name: Coconaut Pomerania ULTRA Trail
description: Coconaut Pomerania ULTRA Trail is a trail-running series held on the hilly trails of Pomerania and Kashubia, with the event base at KJ Barłomino. The event offers five distances: 100 km, 65 km, 42 km, 21 km and 11 km, providing a range of challenges for trail runners. It showcases the beauty of the Kashubian landscape and regional attractions, and participants can look forward to excellent aid stations along the course. The event is supported by the #AktywnaWieś programme and organised by the Pomerania Sports Association.
course_highlights: Hilly trails of Pomerania and Kashubia
Beautiful Kashubian landscapes
Excellent aid stations along the course
additional: The event offers five distances: 100 km, 65 km, 42 km, 21 km and 11 km, as well as the Junior Trail run of up to 1 km. The races take place at KJ Barłomino. The event promotes regional trails and tourist attractions in Pomerania and is supported by the #AktywnaWieś programme. The event is supported by Coconaut and features courses at various difficulty levels, an attractive base in Barłomino and beautiful views of Kashubia.

name: Łemkowyna Trail
location: Krynica-Zdrój, Powiat nowotarski, Lesser Poland Voivodeship, Poland
distance_verbose: Ultramaraton, 100 km, Ultramaraton, 50 km, Maraton, 28 km, 10 km
description: Łemkowyna Trail is a mountain race along a route marked by the Main Beskid Trail in the Low Beskids. The event takes place around Krynica-Zdrój and Komańcza, offering a range of distances from 10 km to a 150 km ultramarathon. The course features substantial elevation gain and challenging natural terrain, making it a test for trail-running and mountain-adventure enthusiasts. The event has a strong tradition and attracts runners from across Poland and abroad.
course_highlights: Route marked by the Main Beskid Trail
Significant elevation changes of up to +5,860 m and -5,970 m on the longest distance
A range of distances from 10 km to 150 km, with time limits
additional: Participants can switch between courses until October 1, 2026. Participant limits for individual distances range from 300 to 550. Starts are scheduled across October 17 and 18, 2026, with different start times for each distance. Each distance has a time limit. The event takes place on natural mountain trails with substantial elevation changes. Courses include elevation gains of up to 740 m for the 30 km and 150 km ultramarathon distances, with time limits of up to 35 hours. Registration is available online, with options for entry-fee refunds and transfer of race packages.

name: Pomerania Ultra-Trail®
description: Pomerania Ultra-Trail® is a series of trail races held on the hilly trails of Pomerania and Kashubia, with the event base at KJ Barłomino. The event offers five distances: 100 km, 65 km, 42 km, 21 km, and 11 km, providing a range of challenges for trail runners. The races showcase the beauty of the Kashubian landscape and regional attractions, and participants can expect well-stocked aid stations along the course. The event is supported by the #AktywnaWieś programme and organised by the Pomerania Sports Association.
course_highlights: Hilly trails of Pomerania and Kashubia
Beautiful Kashubian landscapes
Well-stocked aid stations along the course
additional: The event takes place at KJ Barłomino. Five distances are available: 100 km, 65 km, 42 km, 21 km, and 11 km, as well as a Junior race of up to 1 km. The organiser is the Pomerania Sports Association. The event promotes long-distance trail running and Nordic walking. It is supported by the #AktywnaWieś programme. The event features multiple distances, routes through the beautiful Kashubian landscape, support from #AktywnaWieś, and a base at KJ Barłomino.

name: Dębowiec Nocna Pętla
description: Dębowiec Night Loop is a mountain race on the slopes of Dębowiec in Bielsko-Biała. The 8-kilometre course follows forest trails from Dębowiec to the Wapienica Valley and back. Runners face a demanding climb beneath the Dębowiec cable car, and a bonfire and meal await them at the finish. The race offers a chance to spend an October evening actively, and participants receive a race pack and medals. Prizes are awarded to the top finishers and the oldest participants. A Nordic Walking event is held alongside the race, with a distance of approximately 4 km and a finish at the Dębowiec 520 mountain hostel.
course_highlights: 8 km course on forest trails from Dębowiec to the Wapienica Valley and back
Demanding climb beneath the Dębowiec cable car
Finish at the Dębowiec 520 mountain hostel, with a bonfire and meal
additional: Race participants must bring a headlamp. Sports equipment vouchers will be awarded to the top three finishers in the Open categories and the top three women. Special prizes are planned for the oldest male and female participants. A bonfire is held after the race at the Dębowiec 520 mountain hostel. A free Nordic Walking event is held alongside the race, covering approximately 4 km and starting at 18:00 from the lower station of the Dębowiec cable car. The race route starts at the lower station of the Dębowiec cable car, climbs to a clearing, turns back with a hairpin at the checkpoint, and finishes at the Dębowiec 520 mountain hostel. The Nordic Walking route is 6 km long and passes through Dylówki Pass and Cyberniok. Participants need a headlamp.

name: IV Wilczy Półmaraton
price_range: 100 zł - 130 zł za dystans, 80 zł za koszulkę
description: The IV Wilczy Half Marathon is a unique trail race held in the picturesque, wild forests of the Rybnik Forest District, in the “Głębokie Doły” nature reserve. The approximately 22 km half-marathon route follows unique forest paths, offering runners contact with nature and rare plant species. It is the only half marathon of its kind in Silesia, promising plenty of adrenaline and satisfaction for cross-country enthusiasts. Every participant receives a commemorative medal, and the route is full of amusing, muddy traps. Join us in Wilcza for an unforgettable sporting experience!
course_highlights: An approximately 22 km route through the forests of the Rybnik Forest District
Forest paths in the “Głębokie Doły” nature reserve, with its unique microclimate
Natural muddy traps and wild, picturesque terrain
additional: A commemorative medal for every participant. Dogs are welcome. The race office is located at the Community Centre in Wilcza, Karola Miarki 123. A commemorative T-shirt is available as an optional purchase for PLN 80. The route is approximately 22 km and runs through forest terrain. Participation is available in canicross and Nordic walking. Commemorative medals are provided. Online registration is available, with prices depending on the registration period.

name: Rajd Waligóry
description: Rajd Waligóry is an orienteering event held in the scenic Wiśnickie Foothills near Bochnia. Participants compete by finding checkpoints using a map and compass, combining adventure, exercise, and outdoor fun. The routes vary in length and difficulty, catering to both families and more experienced competitors. The event has a recreational and sporting character and promotes an active lifestyle, as well as exploring local nature and history.
course_highlights: Routes pass through the Wiśnickie Foothills, with charming forest paths and rolling hills
Checkpoints are marked with white-and-orange lanterns equipped with punches
Participants can plan their own routes and choose the order in which to visit the checkpoints
additional: The start and finish are at Arka Cafe in Lanckorona (for the Mini Rajd Waligóry). Participants receive a map before the start and can plan their route and individual start time within the designated hours. There is no official closing ceremony or awards presentation, and results are published on the website. GPS navigation is prohibited on the course; compasses are allowed. orienteering, checkpoints, maps, no GPS navigation

description: The Gliwice Half Marathon is a running event held since 2014 that has become an important fixture on Poland’s running calendar over the past 12 years. The race follows a course that starts and finishes at the PreZero Arena Gliwice Sports and Entertainment Hall. Participants can expect professional organisation, a time limit for completing the course, and support from volunteers and city services. In 2026, the race comes to an end, and the City of Gliwice takes over its organisation, continuing the event’s tradition.
course_highlights: Start and finish at the PreZero Arena Gliwice Sports and Entertainment Hall
Half-marathon course through the streets of Gliwice
Time limit for completing the course: 3 hours
additional: The race office will be open at the PreZero Arena Gliwice Sports and Entertainment Hall on Saturday, 25 October 2025, from 14:00 to 20:00, and on Sunday, 26 October 2025, from 7:00 to 8:00. The time limit for completing the half-marathon is 3 hours from the start. Registration for the event is open, with discount options for participants. The event supports the local community and promotes an active lifestyle.

name: 52.Maraton Dębno 2026
organizer: Ośrodek Sportu i Rekreacji w Dębnie
description: The 52nd Dębno Marathon is the oldest and one of the fastest marathons in Poland, taking place on 18 October 2026. The 42.195 km course, certified by the Polish Athletics Association (PZLA), runs through the streets of Dębno and the surrounding area, offering good conditions for personal bests. The event has a rich tradition dating back to 1966 and attracts both amateur and professional runners from Poland and abroad. Participants can expect professional organisation, numerous refreshment stations and enthusiastic crowd support. The marathon is also an opportunity for the running community to come together and a sporting celebration for the whole family.
course_highlights: A 42.195 km course certified by PZLA
4 laps — two on the Dębno–Dargomyśl–Cychry–Dębno route and two through the streets of Dębno
Surface: asphalt (98%) and cobblestones (2%)
additional: The race starts on J. Słowackiego Street in Dębno. There are timing points every 5 km. The race office is located in the Sports and Rehabilitation Hall at 10 Piłsudskiego Street. The programme includes accompanying events, including concerts and a Holy Mass for the marathon runners. The marathon is part of the “Orły Biegowe” series. Registration is online, and the event also includes races over various distances, on-course support and activities for participants.

name: Wartko!... bez Gaszowice
organizer: Ośrodek Kultury i Sportu w Gaszowicach
description: WARTKO!... Bez Gaszowice is an annual 10 km road race organized by the Culture and Sports Centre in Gaszowice. The event attracts people who enjoy an active lifestyle and promotes sport in the local community. The race takes place in the scenic surroundings of Gaszowice, giving participants the chance to compete and enjoy themselves together. It is open and welcoming to runners of different ability levels.
course_highlights: 10 km road race
The course runs through the scenic areas of Gaszowice
A local sporting event that brings the community together
additional: Race packs can be collected at the race office. The event brings the community together and is held as part of local sporting celebrations. The organizer provides electronic timing. The event is open to runners of different ages and ability levels. It is a family-friendly event, with medals, race packs and traditional food at the finish. Participants over 70 can enter the main race and Nordic walking event free of charge.

description: The 14th Panewnicki Wild Boar Run is a recreational running and Nordic walking event held in the picturesque Panewnickie Forests in Katowice. The event takes place on a loop approximately 4,882 metres long, which participants can complete up to four times, with a time limit of 3 hours. The event promotes an active lifestyle and education about proper conduct in forest areas. Participants can compete individually or in pairs, and the event is open to both recreational runners and athletes affiliated with sports clubs.
course_highlights: A route through the Panewnickie Forests, approximately 4,882 m long
The loop is marked every 1 km
The route can be completed up to 4 times
additional: The time limit for completing the route is 3 hours. Participants over 18 must sign a declaration accepting responsibility for their participation or provide a medical certificate. Minors must be accompanied by a parent or guardian during check-in. Entry fees are non-refundable, but may be transferred to a subsequent start, provided the request is submitted by 3:00 p.m. on the Thursday before the event. The event is open to recreational runners and sports clubs, with annual packages available for purchase. The route is approximately 4,882 m long and the time limit is 3 hours.

name: XVII Półmaraton Ziemi Puckiej
location: Stadion Miejski w Pucku, Puck, Puck County, Poland
description: The 17th Puck Land Half Marathon is a well-known running event in Pomerania, returning in 2026 in a refreshed format under the STONE TRI & RUN banner. The event takes place on an updated course in an autumn setting, making it an ideal way to round off the running season. It features a half marathon, a 5 km run, and a 5 km Nordic walking event, all with individual starts. It’s a great opportunity to spend time actively in the beautiful Kashubian region and experience the sporting atmosphere of the Puck Running Triad.
course_highlights: Updated half-marathon course through the scenic Kashubian region
Autumn conditions that are ideal for runners
Final event in the Puck Running Triad
additional: The event features three competitions: a half marathon, a 5 km run, and a 5 km Nordic walking event, all with individual starts. The organizers ensure the courses are professionally prepared, clearly marked, and secured. The event is part of the STONE TRI & RUN series, which promotes an active lifestyle and a family-friendly sporting atmosphere in Kashubia. Asphalt course; start and finish at the Municipal Stadium in Puck; final event in the Puck Running Triad; registration from 12 December 2025 to 12 October 2026.

description: Nocna Ściema is a unique night marathon and half marathon held in Koszalin, known for its excellent atmosphere and distinctive nighttime ambience. The course consists of laps of approximately 7 kilometres, completed multiple times depending on the chosen distance. The race has official PZLA certification, which verifies the course distance and makes it possible to set world records. This is the sixteenth edition of the event, attracting runners who want to improve their personal bests in the one-of-a-kind conditions of a night race.
course_highlights: The course consists of laps of approximately 7 km, completed 3 or 6 times
Official PZLA certification confirms the course distance
Views of the stadium along the course and Koszalin’s undulating terrain
additional: The race office for children and young people opens at around 19:00, with a limited number of places (20). The race office for adults is located in the Koszalin University of Technology Sports Hall at ul. Racławicka, about 300 m from the stadium, and remains open until 30 minutes before the start. Participants must show a photo ID when collecting their race number. The course runs along the streets of Koszalin, with views of exhibits at the aviation museum. The medal and merchandise are updated each year and are an important part of the event. The event offers different distances, including a marathon and half marathon, with reports, photo and video galleries, and options to register online or at the race office. Participants can look forward to attractive prizes and the chance to compete in various themed categories.

name: Chwałowicki Maraton Napoleoński
organizer: Stowarzyszenie na rzecz Rozwoju i Integracji Chwałowic, Arka Tołłoczko, Rafał Malitkowski
description: The Chwałowice Napoleonic Marathon is a small-scale marathon held in the picturesque village of Chwałowice, surrounded by forests and fields. The 42.195 km course follows forest and rural roads in a peaceful, uncrowded setting, with course markings and convenient access. The event is organized by local runners, who prioritize a friendly atmosphere and a recreational experience over competition and prizes. It is an excellent choice for fans of cross-country running in natural surroundings.
course_highlights: A 42.195 km course along forest and rural roads
Start and finish on Polna Street in Chwałowice
Every kilometre marked, with convenient parking
additional: No crowds and a relaxed atmosphere without the pressure of competition. The course is laid out and marked by the “Harcownik” Running Club. Participants can take part in a series of four marathons per year on the same course. The event is friendly and recreational in nature. Napoleonic Marathon, mainly urban parkland terrain, training preparations, online registration, various distances, entries, regulations, GPX routes.

name: Sopot Półmaraton
description: Sopot Half Marathon is an annual half-marathon held in the picturesque seaside city of Sopot. Participants can run a route through charming parts of the city, finishing at ERGO Arena, which offers a unique atmosphere and comfort. The event attracts runners from all over Poland, offering professional organization and attractive race packs. It’s a great opportunity to experience the excitement of sport in the Pearl of the Baltic and earn a commemorative medal and T-shirt.
course_highlights: The route passes through central Sopot and the seaside promenades
The finish is located at ERGO Arena
Picturesque views of the Baltic Sea and Sopot’s iconic pier
additional: The race pack includes an official T-shirt and medal. The half-marathon route is certified and passes through central Sopot and the seaside promenades. The finish is inside ERGO Arena, providing comfortable conditions for runners after the race. Race packs available from 10 February 2026; participant limit: 3,500; discounts for holders of the Sopot Card; the event is part of the Korona Półmaratonów Pomorza 2026–2030 series.

description: The 14th Vistula River Run along the Lower Vistula Valley Trail is an annual race held in Tczew County. Participants can choose between two distances: a certified 42.195 km marathon and an uncertified 21.097 km half marathon. The routes pass through the scenic Lower Vistula Valley and feature a mix of asphalt and gravel surfaces. The race takes place with restricted vehicle traffic. The marathon starts in Tczew at 9:00, and the half marathon starts in Małe Walichnowy at 11:00. Both finish in Tczew.
course_highlights: PZLA-certified 42.195 km marathon through Tczew and nearby towns
21.097 km half marathon on an asphalt-and-gravel route
The route is marked every 1 km with painted markings and yellow signs
additional: The limit is 400 paid participants. The start line closes 15 minutes after the start. The marathon route is PZLA-certified; the half marathon is not. The finish is at the School Complex of Construction and Clothing in Tczew, ul. Bałdowska 19. The routes have varied surfaces. The participant limit is 400, registration is online, and the event includes a half marathon and a marathon.

name: XLIV Perła Paprocan
description: The Perła Paprocan Run is a unique marathon around Paprocany Lake in Tychy, combining competition with training over almost any distance. Runners can complete one or more laps of the 7-kilometre loop, up to the full marathon distance. The event is recreational and community-oriented, promoting a healthy lifestyle and a welcoming atmosphere among runners. Tychy is the only city in Poland where a marathon is held twice a year, and Perła Paprocan is one of those editions.
course_highlights: A 7 km loop around Paprocany Lake
Paved sections (over 50%), as well as compacted paths and forest trails
A refreshment point with drinks, fruit, and sweets available after each lap
additional: Start and finish at the Paprocany Holiday Centre, ul. Parkowa 17, Tychy. Race bibs can be collected in the days before the event and on race day. The participant limit is 1111. Runners do not need to declare their distance before the race and can change it during the event. Participants aged 12 and over may take part with the written consent of a parent or guardian. Valuables can be left in the baggage deposit. The event is recreational, and runners must keep to one half of the paths to allow others to overtake. Participation from age 12 with a guardian’s consent, refreshment points with drinks and fruit, a limit of 1111 participants, online registration, and an event held twice a year.

description: The 146th Gliwice Park Run Provocation is an annual running event held in a city park in Gliwice. The event combines sport, a friendly atmosphere, and contact with nature, offering an opportunity for both experienced runners and those who want to spend time outdoors without the pressure of competition. The race traditionally starts in the clearing behind Piast Stadium, and the event office opens at 9:00. It’s a great opportunity to end February actively and enter the upcoming spring season with renewed energy.

The course suits both experienced runners and amateurs
additional: The event office is open from 9:00. Advance registration and an entry fee are required to be classified. The event takes place in a green urban setting, encouraging social connection and recreation. The race takes place on 31 October 2026, starting in the clearing behind Piast Stadium; online registration is available.

The event is a great opportunity to test your fitness over a middle distance, and participants can use training plans tailored to different experience levels. It is aimed at runners looking for a challenge and the chance to prepare optimally for race day with guidance from experts.

Preparation options with training plans lasting 8 to 20 weeks

description: Gorlicki Mountain Run is an annual running event held in the scenic surroundings of Radocyna and Magura Małastowska in the Low Beskids. The event offers three distances: 7.6 km, 23.9 km, and a 2.3 km Vertical race with significant elevation gain. It attracts both amateurs and elite runners, offering a unique atmosphere and cash prizes. The participant limit is 400, and the start and finish are located at the State Forests Holiday Resort “Radocyna” and Magura Ski Park. This is the event’s eleventh edition, combining sporting competition with the beauty of mountain nature.
course_highlights: 24 km course with 610 m of elevation gain
7 km course with 160 m of elevation gain
2.3 km Vertical with 340 m of elevation gain to Magura Małastowska
additional: Participant limit: 400 (150 for 7 km, 250 for 24 km). Start and finish at the State Forests Holiday Resort “Radocyna.” Race office open from 7:45 to 10:00. The time limit for the 24 km race is 5 hours. Runners must attach their bibs to the front of their shirt or shorts. Participants with a Rate My Trail ranking of 730 points or higher may enter free of charge. The courses include mountain trails and muddy sections, and the start is scheduled for 10:30. The event attracts both amateurs and experienced trail runners.

description: Marceliński Autumn Run 2026 is a cross-country race organized in Poznań by running enthusiasts from the Biegi.Wlkp. group. The event takes place on scenic courses that showcase the location’s aesthetic appeal. Since 2014, the organizers have focused on promoting cross-country running in Wielkopolska, offering participants a unique running experience in beautiful natural surroundings.

Courses that showcase the location’s aesthetic appeal
Organized by experienced running enthusiasts from Wielkopolska

name: 14. PKO Bieg Niepodległości w Rzeszowie
description: The 14th PKO Independence Run in Rzeszów is an annual running event organized by the Rzeszów Running Club “Rzeszów Biega,” in partnership with the Rzeszów City Hall and PKO Bank Polski. The 10 km main race starts and finishes at Rzeszów Market Square and takes place on November 11 at 11:11. The event promotes an active lifestyle and running in the Podkarpackie region, offering age-group classifications and special categories, including for doctors and lawyers. Participants receive a race pack with a T-shirt, bib number and chip, and a commemorative medal at the finish. The participant limit is 3,000, and entrants must confirm they are fit to run by providing a medical certificate or declaration.
course_highlights: The 10 km main race starts and finishes at Rzeszów Market Square
Separate age-group classifications and special categories, including for doctors and lawyers
Participant limit of 3,000; race pack includes a T-shirt, bib number and chip
additional: Medal engraving is available for an additional fee of 30 zł. The number of race packs available on race day is limited, and the entry fee is non-refundable. Participants must be over 16 (minors require parental or guardian consent). Participants receive race packs containing a T-shirt, bib number and chip. The course is marked every 1 km, and the event includes warm-ups and refreshment stations along the course. Wearing the organizer’s T-shirt is mandatory.

name: 36. Bieg Niepodległości w Warszawie
description: The 35th Independence Run in Warsaw is an annual running event held to celebrate National Independence Day. The main 10 km race takes place on the streets of the capital, with the start and finish on Jana Pawła II Avenue. The event attracts both experienced runners and amateurs, and also offers a Nordic walking category and the accompanying Independence Mile, covering 1,918 m. The main race starts in waves to ensure participants’ comfort and safety. The organizers provide a varied program and efficient race services, including convenient pre-race bib collection dates.
course_highlights: A 10 km route through Warsaw certified by the PZLA
Start and finish on Jana Pawła II Avenue, level with Miła Street
Wave starts for the main race, with runners divided into zones according to their expected finish time
additional: The main race starts at 11:11, with wave starts divided into time zones. The Independence Mile starts at 10:00. Athletes using active wheelchairs, handbikes, and tandems start at 11:08. Race bibs can be collected at Westfield Arkadia from November 7–10. On race day, the race office is closed, except for package collection by participants from outside Warsaw between 8:00 and 10:00. Participants are asked to line up at the start wearing white or red shirts to form a red-and-white flag. The route is well-known and popular, and around 20,000 people take part in the event. The event includes various running categories, including the main race, Nordic walking, and virtual options available until November 17. In previous years, the event was the largest running event in Poland.

description: The Poznań Independence Run – I Love Poland! is a cross-country race held in picturesque locations in Poznań, particularly in Strzeszyn near Malibu Beach. The event is part of the activities of a group of running enthusiasts who have been promoting cross-country running in Greater Poland since 2014, with an emphasis on attractive courses and the sporting character of the event. The race has a patriotic dimension and takes place on 11 November, combining sport with a celebration of Poland’s independence. Runners are invited to take part in a range of distances amid beautiful natural surroundings.
course_highlights: Cross-country course around Strzeszyn and Malibu Beach
Picturesque green areas of Poznań
A patriotic race held on 11 November
additional: The organiser is a group of running enthusiasts from Greater Poland, active since 2014 and specialising in cross-country races. The race takes place in the green areas of Strzeszyn, near Malibu Beach. The event has a patriotic character and is part of the Poznań Running Triad. Participant limit: 750; picturesque courses; cross-country races.

name: 10 Bieg Niepodległości z wąsem
location: Stadion Olimpijski, Wrocław, Lower Silesian Voivodeship, Poland
description: The Wrocław Independence Day Run with a Mustache is an annual running event held at the Olympic Stadium in Wrocław, commemorating the 107th anniversary of Poland regaining independence. Participants can choose between the 10 km and 5 km distances, and the main race course is certified by the PZLA. The race takes place on roads closed to traffic, and runners receive a medal and a post-race meal at the finish. Free accompanying runs are available for younger participants, and runners can purchase a high-quality technical T-shirt featuring the race logo.
course_highlights: The PZLA-certified 10 km course consists of two 5 km loops
Start and finish at the Pergola at the Olympic Stadium
The course follows asphalt and gravel roads at the foot of the flood embankments
additional: Race packs can be collected from the race office at the Olympic Stadium on November 10 and 11. The pack contains a race number, mustache-patterned socks, a stick-on mustache, sponsor products, a calendar, a T-shirt (if ordered), a medal, and a post-race meal. There is a hydration station on the course. The race takes place on roads closed to traffic. Free accompanying runs are organized for children. Technical T-shirts can be ordered until 16.10.2025 for 90 zł. Changing rooms and a bag deposit are available on site. The 5 km race starts at 10:11 and the 10 km race at 11:11. The race takes place on roads closed to traffic; accompanying runs for children are available; T-shirts can be purchased through the registration form on datasport; participants receive medals; on-the-day registration is available.

name: 9 Olsztyński Bieg Niepodległości
location: Centrum Rekreacyjno-Sportowe Ukiel, Olsztyn, Warmian-Masurian Voivodeship, Poland
description: The Olsztyn Independence Run is an annual patriotic sporting event held in Olsztyn, combining the joy of running with celebrations of Independence Day. The event is open to everyone, from experienced runners to families with children. The races take place at the Ukiel Recreation and Sports Centre and include 5 km and 10 km runs, Nordic walking, and children’s races of up to 400 metres. The atmosphere is lively despite the autumn weather, and places are limited, with online registration open until 6 November.
course_highlights: The 5 km and 10 km routes run through the Ukiel Recreation and Sports Centre grounds and along nearby streets: Sielska, Schumana and Kapitańska
The event combines sporting competition with patriotic celebrations
Nordic walking and children’s races of up to 400 metres are also available
additional: The start and finish are located at the Ukiel Recreation and Sports Centre. The event takes place on 11 November, and registration is open online until 6 November. Participants can choose from the 5 km and 10 km runs, Nordic walking, and children’s races of up to 400 m. Traffic disruptions should be expected along the race route. Traffic disruptions along the route; start at 9:00; registration until 6 November; event at the Ukiel Recreation and Sports Centre and on Sielska, Schumana and Kapitańska streets.

name: Gdyński Bieg Niepodległości
description: The Gdynia Independence Run is an annual running event held in Gdynia and part of the 2026 Gdynia Grand Prix. The 10 km main race attracts runners of all ages, and there are also races for children and young people. The event combines sport and recreation, with participants able to expect professional organization and an atmosphere celebrating Poland’s independence. Photos and video footage are taken during the event for the organizers’ promotional purposes.
course_highlights: 10 km main race
Races for children and young people
Part of the 2026 Gdynia Grand Prix
additional: Photos and video footage will be taken during the event to promote events organized by GCS and the Municipality of the City of Gdynia. Registration until October 28, 2026; results, photo galleries, and information about event partners are available.

name: II Bieg Legionów Polskich
description: The 2nd Polish Legions Run commemorates the anniversary of Poland regaining its independence and offers two distances: 5 km and 10 km. The starts take place in scenic coastal locations: Władysławowo, Rozewie and Jastrzębia Góra. The organizer provides transport from Jastrzębia Góra to the start locations and opens the race office on the day before and on race day. The course is available online, allowing participants to familiarize themselves with the route before the start.
course_highlights: The course passes through Władysławowo, Rozewie and Jastrzębia Góra
The 10 km race starts by the General Haller monument on Morska Street in Władysławowo
The 5 km race starts by the bust of Marshal Piłsudski on Garnizonowa Street in Rozewie
additional: Transport from Jastrzębia Góra to the start locations is provided. The race office is open on 10 November 2025 from 14:30 to 15:30 at OSiR Władysławowo, and on 11 November 2025 from 10:20 to 10:50 in Jastrzębia Góra. The course is available online at https://www.traseo.pl/trasa/bieg-legionow-polskich. Registration runs from 22 September to 5 November 2025; the event takes place on routes with moderate elevation gain, starting in Władysławowo and Rozewie.

name: XIV Bieg Niepodległości
description: The 14th Independence Run is an annual 10 km road race held in Rzeszów, promoting an active lifestyle and running in the Podkarpacie region. The start and finish are at Rzeszów Market Square, and the race takes place on November 11, Poland’s Independence Day. Runners compete in multiple age categories and special classifications, including those for doctors and lawyers. Participants receive a race pack containing a T-shirt, race number and chip, and a commemorative medal at the finish. The participant limit is 3,000, and entrants must confirm they are fit to run by providing a medical certificate or a declaration.
course_highlights: A 10 km road race starting and finishing at Market Square in Rzeszów
Separate age-group and special classifications (e.g. doctors and the legal profession)
A commemorative medal for every participant at the finish
additional: The participant limit is 3,000. Participants must be at least 16 years old on race day. Minors may participate with the consent of a parent or legal guardian. The race pack contains a T-shirt, race number and chip. Medal engraving is available for an additional fee of 30 zł. The entry fee is non-refundable. On race day, race packs are available only for cash and in limited quantities. Participants can expect a clearly marked course, detailed safety regulations, and information about registration and participant limits. The race takes place in Rytro, and the event is part of the National Independence Day celebrations.

description: The Kościan County Grand Prix is a series of five 5 km races, organized by all the municipalities in Kościan County under the patronage of the Kościan County Governor. Its aim is to promote physical activity, healthy competition, and community integration. Residents of the county who turn 16 in 2025 may participate. Each race requires a separate entry fee, and the overall standings are based on the total points earned across the races.
course_highlights: A series of five 5 km races
Organized by all the municipalities in Kościan County
Separate standings for women and men, with no age categories
additional: Participation in the Grand Prix is free; only the entry fee for each individual race, set locally, is payable. The races are scheduled from June to December 2025 in various locations across the county. Points from the individual races are added together, with prizes for the top 6 women and top 6 men, as well as additional special prizes from the organizers of the individual races. The series comprises five 5 km races held from June to December, with overall standings and prizes for the top finishers. The main 10 km race is scheduled for 15 November 2026 in Kościerzyna, with typical autumn weather and possible rain.

name: XXIV Maraton Odrzański
description: The 24th Odra Marathon is a race held in Kędzierzyn-Koźle and organized by the Odra Consortium Foundation. The event offers two categories: a full marathon of 42.195 km and a half marathon of 21.097 km. It is a sporting and recreational event, with the Municipal Sports and Recreation Centre in Kędzierzyn-Koźle as its partner. The race office operates on the days before the race and on race day, providing support for participants.
course_highlights: Marathon and half-marathon courses in Kędzierzyn-Koźle
Organized by the Odra Consortium Foundation
In partnership with the Municipal Sports and Recreation Centre
additional: The race office is open on 14.11.2025 from 17:00 to 19:00 and on 15.11.2025 from 7:00 to 8:30. Organizers' telephone contacts: Piotr (+48) 500 028 811, Piotr (+48) 604 589 483, Ania (+48) 602 534 780. The event's partner is the Municipal Sports and Recreation Centre in Kędzierzyn-Koźle. Electronic timekeeping; a 6-hour time limit; the event includes both a marathon and a half marathon and takes place in November in Kędzierzyn-Koźle.

description: The Silesian Voivodeship Orienteering Walks Cup is a series of events organized by tourism clubs and groups across Silesia. Competitions take place in different rounds throughout the year, with participants competing in six age categories and a team classification. The “First Snow” round is the tenth edition of the cup in the 2026 season and will take place on November 21 in Katowice. The event combines sporting competition with spending active time outdoors and navigating the terrain.
course_highlights: Orienteering walks across the Silesian Voivodeship
Competition in six age categories
Team classification and cups for the top participants
additional: The event includes different age categories, is part of an orienteering event series, and takes place in forested and urban areas in Katowice.

The race attracts both experienced runners and younger participants, offering sporting competition and a friendly atmosphere.

The race takes place on a loop approximately 4,882 metres long, which participants can complete up to four times. The event promotes an active lifestyle and education about appropriate conduct in forest areas. Participants can compete individually or in pairs, and the event is open to both recreational runners and members of sports clubs.

organizer: Miejski Zarząd Usług Komunalnych w Gliwicach
description: The 146th Gliwice Park Run Provocation is an annual running event held in Gliwice, combining sport, a friendly atmosphere and time among the city’s green spaces. The run is open to both experienced runners and people who want to spend time actively without the pressure of competition. The start traditionally takes place in the clearing behind the Piast Stadium, and participants can look forward to a welcoming atmosphere and an active way to wrap up February. The event is a great opportunity to start a new month with energy and in a good mood.
course_highlights: Start in the clearing behind Piast Stadium (entrance from Leśna Street)
The route passes through the city’s green spaces
The event combines sport, a friendly atmosphere and recreation
additional: The event office is open from 9:00. To be included in the results, advance registration and an entry fee are required. The event takes place on the last day of February, making it a great way to end the month actively. trail run, online registration, start and finish in the clearing behind Piast Stadium

name: Jesienny Ultra Świr
description: Jesienny Ultra Świr is a mountain ultramarathon held in Grybów, offering a challenge for fans of long-distance running in natural terrain. The course runs mainly along forest and gravel paths, with minimal asphalt, providing an authentic trail-running experience. The event offers different competition formats, including timed races and Nordic Walking, catering to various levels of experience. It is organised by experienced enthusiasts who ensure a welcoming atmosphere and participants’ safety.
course_highlights: 98% of the course runs along forest and gravel paths
Minimal asphalt: just 2%
Start and finish at the Winter Sports Centre in Ptaszkowa
additional: The start, finish and race office are at the Winter Sports Centre in Ptaszkowa. On race day, the race office is open from 06:45 to 07:30 for the 6/12/24-hour distances and until 09:30 for Nordic Walking and the one-lap race. In the 6-hour and 12-hour races, the winner is the participant who completes the greatest number of full 17 km laps. Running is prohibited during the Nordic Walking event, and judges on the course monitor proper technique. Participants must check in at the race office with an identity document and have the mandatory equipment. The event is part of the Jesienny Ultra Świr series, which includes various distances and activity formats, with online registration. The course may be changed due to weather conditions.

name: XXIII Maraton Komandosa
description: The XXIII Commandos Marathon is a demanding 42.195 km marathon held in Lubliniec. The race takes place on 28 November 2026 and is organised by the Wojskowy Klub Biegacza „Meta” Lubliniec. The course has recently been changed and is available online. Participants can expect professional timekeeping and full technical support for the event.
course_highlights: The new course is available online
Marathon distance: 42.195 km
Organiser: Wojskowy Klub Biegacza „Meta” Lubliniec
additional: The race office is open on 28 November from 15:00 to 20:30 and on 29 November from 07:00 to 08:40. The entry fee can only be paid via an individual link to quick online payments through tpay.com, sent by email. After 31 October 2026, entry is possible only with the organiser’s consent and without the full race package. The participant limit has been reached and registration is suspended. New course; participant limit reached; urban and forest terrain; electronic timekeeping.

name: 45 Strzeliński Rogaining
location: Kamiennik, Strzelin County, Lower Silesian Voivodeship, Poland
organizer: Polskie Towarzystwo Turystyczno-Krajoznawcze Oddział Ziemi Strzelińskiej
description: Strzeliński Rogaining is a walking orienteering event in which teams of 2–5 plan their own route to visit as many checkpoints as possible within a set time. The checkpoints are spread across the terrain and marked on a map. The event is open to participants of different ages and experience levels, from enthusiasts and recreational participants to families. Rogaining combines tourism and sport, and participants can modify their route at any time during the competition, making it an appealing way to enjoy the outdoors. The event is organised by the Polish Tourist and Sightseeing Society, Strzelin District Branch, which has been holding orienteering competitions in the region for many years.
course_highlights: Teams travel on foot only, using a map and compass to navigate the terrain
Checkpoints have different point values depending on how difficult they are to find
Participants can choose and change their own route, at any length from 5 to 70 km
additional: The competition is open to all age groups and genders. Teams consist of 2–5 people. Rogaining combines tourism and sport and is suitable for both experienced competitors and families. Routes can be changed during the competition. In 2026, four rogaining events are planned around Strzelin, including the 45th edition in November. The events offer distances from 5 km to 70 km and use maps and compasses. They cater to different experience levels and offer both recreational and competitive participation.

name: Szybka Piątka
description: Szybka Piątka is a 5 km race held in Lublin on 29 November 2026. The event is part of a series of races organized by the Sports Development Foundation in Lublin, which promotes physical activity and the integration of the local community. The race is an excellent opportunity for runners of all levels to test their fitness and enjoy the city’s sporting atmosphere.
course_highlights: A 5 km route through the city
Training support for 8 to 20 weeks
Organized by a local sports foundation
additional: The race is part of local sporting events and includes various distances and age categories, as well as the Lublin Grand Prix classifications.

name: Garmin Ultra Race Gdansk
description: Garmin Ultra Race Gdańsk is an exceptional trail race taking place on 5 December 2026 in the picturesque Tricity Landscape Park. The course combines a seaside atmosphere with varied, mountainous terrain, offering runners challenging climbs, valleys, ravines and gorges. It is a great opportunity to end the season amid sporting competition and close contact with nature. The event is part of a nationwide mountain-running series that promotes physical activity and respect for the environment.
course_highlights: The course runs through the Tricity Landscape Park, close to the sea
Varied terrain with dense forests, valleys, ravines and gorges
Challenging elevation gains and natural climbs characteristic of trail running
additional: Race packs can be collected on 4–5 December 2026 at the race office. Starts are held in waves: the 6 km night race starts at 19:00 on 4 December; on 5 December, the 101 km (05:00), 53 km (07:45), 27 km (10:30) and 12 km (13:30) races start, along with Garmin Junior races for children. Time limits for completing the distances range from 2 to 15 hours, depending on course length. Discounts are available when registering for more than one event in the series. The participant card is available 5 days before the race after logging in to startlist.pl. Distances from 12 km to 86 km, time limits, qualifying points for Ultra Trail du Mont Blanc, and accompanying races for children and young people.

name: XVII Grand Prix Mysłowic
description: The 17th Mysłowice Grand Prix is a series of races organized by the Truchtacz Mysłowice Association, promoting a healthy, active lifestyle and bringing together runners of all abilities. The event takes place in Mysłowice and is open to all age groups and running levels. Participants can expect a friendly atmosphere and the opportunity to compete throughout the Grand Prix series. Registration is available only at the Race Office on race day, and participation is free.
course_highlights: 10 km race in the scenic surroundings of Mysłowice
A series of seasonal events promoting a healthy lifestyle
A running community and opportunities to connect with the local community
additional: Registration for the Grand Prix series is available only at the Race Office on race day. Participation in the Grand Prix races is free. The event is open to everyone, regardless of age or ability. It focuses on promoting physical activity, health, and the running community, with varied courses and seasonal editions.

The route follows one or two loops through Studzienice Forest, part of the Pszczyna Forest, offering scenic woodland views. The event features several distances, including the Fancy Dress Run, children’s races, 6 km and 12 km runs and Nordic Walking, as well as a half marathon and marathon. Participants can expect medals, awards for costumes, and traditional pea soup at the finish.

Races cover one or two forest loops
Scenic woodland views and natural mud

GPX files are available for the half-marathon, marathon, and 6 km and 12 km routes. New marathon distance, changed start and finish location, food and recovery attractions, honorary patronages, additional cross-country races, and team classification.

description: Bieg po Moczkę i Makówki is an annual, friendly running event held in Stanowice. Since 2012, it has become a fixture on the holiday running calendar. The course is 10 km long, divided into four 2.5 km loops, and runners may finish after any number of loops. After the run, participants receive handmade gingerbread medals and traditional moczka and makówki, and can also enjoy hot coffee and tea. The event has a relaxed, friendly atmosphere, with a prize-winning contest for the most interesting costume and a spectator competition.

The event attracts hundreds of runners and hiking enthusiasts from across Poland every year, offering a distinctive atmosphere and beautiful views. The organizers look after participants’ safety and comfort, providing refreshment and checkpoint stations along the routes.

description: Pietrasze Cross Country is a series of cross-country races held in the picturesque Pietrasze Forest in Białystok. The course is entirely natural and highly varied, featuring forest trails, uphill and downhill sections, and different surfaces such as forest floor, grass, sand, and mud. The race requires versatility and good fitness from participants, with volunteers and lead cyclists present along the course. After the race, participants can socialize over music, doughnuts, and tea, adding to the event’s friendly atmosphere.
course_highlights: A course entirely on varied, natural forest terrain
Numerous climbs and descents, with a total elevation gain of 140 m+
The course is marked with blue-and-white tape, with lead cyclists and volunteers present

description: The 5th Jedlina-Zdrój Mountain Festival is a mountain running event taking place on 10 May 2026 in Jedlina-Zdrój. Participants can choose from three distances: 10 km, 23.5 km and 50 km. The start and finish are at Jedlinka Palace. The route runs through the scenic Wałbrzych Mountains, including Borowa Mountain, which has a newly built observation tower, and features challenging climbs and varied terrain. The event is a great opportunity to enjoy an active break and discover the charms of the region.
course_highlights: The route passes over Borowa Mountain, with its new observation tower
Varied terrain: gravel roads, asphalt roads, forest trails and mountain paths
Distances of 10 km, 23.5 km and an ultra 50 km, with refreshment and timing checkpoints
additional: The total participant limit is 600. Festival T-shirts can be ordered until 19.04.2026 for 90 zł; they are made from high-quality Attiq technical fabric. The 50 km ultra route has 7 refreshment stations and 5 timing checkpoints. The start and finish are at Jedlinka Palace, ul. Zamkowa 4. The organizer reserves the right to modify the route up to one week before the start. The mountain route is demanding and features varied terrain. There is a limit of 600 participants, online registration, possible date changes in the event of sanitary restrictions, accommodation options and festival T-shirts for participants.

name: Garmin Ultra Race Myślenice 2026
description: Garmin Ultra Race Myślenice is a mountain trail race taking place on 9 May 2026 in the picturesque Beskid Wyspowy mountains, near Kraków. The routes run along forest trails with numerous steep climbs and breathtaking views, offering challenges for runners of varying experience levels. Myślenice combines natural beauty, history and modern infrastructure, making the race an attractive event for fans of active recreation. The Garmin Ultra Race series promotes running in harmony with nature, fair play and support for the running community.
course_highlights: Forest trails in the Beskid Wyspowy mountains, with natural climbs
Views of the Tatras from selected points along the route
A range of distances from 13 km to 78 km, with up to 2,300 m of elevation gain
additional: Race packs can be collected at the race office on 8–9 May. Starts are in waves according to distance, with the longest distance, 78 km, starting at 05:00. The time limit for completing the 78 km distance is 15 hours. Discounts are available when registering for more than one event in the series. Runner cards can be downloaded 5 days before the race after logging in to startlist.pl. Award ceremonies take place after each distance has finished. Distances from 6 km to 101 km; time limits from 1 hour to 17.5 hours; different race-pack options; the option to take part in several distances as part of the Challenge; mountain terrain; medical support; marked routes; refreshment stations; GPS tracker (78 km only).

name: Bieg Herosa
description: Bieg Herosa is a unique running event held in Klucze near Olkusz, offering a range of distances and race formats on challenging sandy terrain. The most extreme event is Nomada 9h, where runners take on desert sand and their own limits for 9 hours, relying on strategy and endurance. Shorter options are also available, including Nomada 3h, dynamic 5- and 7-kilometre loops, children’s races, and special races with dogs that highlight cooperation and trust between the handler and their four-legged companion. It’s an event for those seeking a sporting challenge and a connection with nature in a unique desert setting.
course_highlights: Sandy, desert terrain that demands good technique and endurance
Long-distance competition lasting up to 9 hours in extreme conditions
Special courses for dog-running races and children’s races over distances from 200 to 1,000 metres
additional: The event includes various race formats: an extreme 9-hour race, a 3-hour race, short 5- and 7-kilometre loops, children’s races, and races with dogs, which require cooperation and trust between the runner and their pet. The event focuses on pushing personal limits, endurance, and strategy in challenging terrain.

description: Blue Power Run is an inclusive race organised for people on the autism spectrum, their families and friends. The event aims to support social inclusion through a shared sporting event that brings participants together and raises awareness of autism. The race takes place on a paved path by Arkonka Swimming Area in Szczecin. Above all, taking part is about the satisfaction of completing the challenge and overcoming yourself, regardless of finishing place. The event also includes group activities led by therapists and volunteers, further encouraging inclusion.
course_highlights: The route follows a paved path by Arkonka Swimming Area
An inclusive race for people on the autism spectrum and their families
Group activities led by therapists and volunteers
additional: The entry limit is 300 participants. Race packs can be collected at the Race Office on Friday, 16 May, from 10:00 to 12:00 and from 14:00 to 16:00, as well as on event day from 12:00 to 13:00. Starts are divided into age categories, with distances ranging from 200 to 600 metres. The Race Office and start are located by the Szyszka restaurant. The event is inclusive, with routes for children and adults, and takes place on a paved course in Arkonka. Online registration is available until 10 May 2025. The start is scheduled for 13:00.

In addition to the main race, children’s and youth races are held over distances suited to different age groups. Participants in the main race receive a race pack containing items from sponsors as well as informational and promotional materials.

Runners must keep to the right on the course. Classifications include overall categories for women and men and age categories for adults and children. description: Rajd Beskidy Short is a European adventure race held in the scenic Beskids, on the border between Poland and Slovakia. The event includes a variety of disciplines, such as mountain biking, trekking, kayaking, climbing and orienteering, with routes through mountainous terrain featuring beautiful views and challenging sections. The race is open to two-person teams or solo participants, offering an intense challenge for lovers of adventure and outdoor sports. The start and finish are in the Kosice area, and the organizers provide professional service and support.

The race includes various disciplines, such as climbing, kayaking, navigation and field tasks, and the route passes through scenic areas of the Polish mountains, including caves and rock formations.

name: VIII Ultramaraton Warmiński Warneland
description: The VIII Warmian Ultramarathon Warneland is a unique running event held in picturesque Olsztyn. The route follows charming trails in Warmia, along the Łyna River and Lake Ukiel, offering runners a chance to connect with nature and enjoy beautiful views. The event is a great opportunity to spend time actively, both for experienced ultramarathon runners and younger running enthusiasts, who can take part in the Ultra Warmiaczek children’s races. The atmosphere encourages participants to connect and share a sporting adventure.
course_highlights: Picturesque trails in Warmia around Olsztyn
Route along the Łyna River and Lake Ukiel
A chance to connect with nature and enjoy charming views
additional: Race packs can be collected on 9 May 2026 from 17:00 to 21:00 at the Best Western Plus Olsztyn Old Town Hotel, and from 07:30 to 10:00 at CRS Ukiel for the children’s races. The W50+ and W25+ distances start at 08:00. The time limit for completing the W50+ race is 10 hours, and for W25+ it is 5 hours. After this time, runners must leave the course and remove their race bibs. The Ultra Warmiaczek children’s races start at 11:10. The race village is located at the Ukiel Recreation and Sports Centre, close to numerous hotels and apartments. The event features distances of 53 km, 32 km and 19 km, as well as children’s races, with time limits of 10 and 5 hours. The start and finish are at CRS Ukiel in Olsztyn. Participants can expect medical and logistical support, and registration closes on 26 April 2025.

name: Wings for Life 2026 Gdańsk Południe
description: The Wings for Life World Run is a unique global race held simultaneously around the world. Instead of a traditional finish line, participants race against a virtual Catcher Car, which starts 30 minutes after the runners and gradually increases its speed until it catches the last participant. In Gdańsk Południe, the race will take place on May 10, 2026, starting at 13:00 near the Parkrun Gdańsk-Poludnie finish area. The course is an approximately 3 km loop on a paved surface, with a minimal uphill section on the connector. All entry fees support spinal cord research.
course_highlights: An approximately 3 km walking and running loop
Paved surface, uneven in places near the large reservoir
A minimal uphill section on the connector toward the smaller reservoir
additional: The race is open to runners and participants using wheelchairs. The Catcher Car starts 30 minutes after the runners at a speed of 14 km/h and gradually speeds up. 100% of entry fees go toward spinal cord research. Participants use the Wings for Life World Run app to follow the race and results. The race starts at 13:00, and participants use the app to register and track their progress. The event is open to runners and wheelchair users.

name: Wings for Life World Run 2026 Poznań
description: The Wings for Life World Run is a unique global race in which all participants start at the same time around the world, running from the Catcher Car. There is no traditional finish line—participants run until they are caught by the car. All entry fees go towards research into treatments for spinal cord injuries, making this not only a sporting challenge but also a charity event. You can take part locally or via the app, which lets you run from anywhere in the world.
course_highlights: Simultaneous start around the world
No traditional finish line—the Catcher Car pursues participants
A race for runners, wheelchair users and first-timers
additional: Participants can join the race locally or via the Wings for Life World Run app, which tracks time and distance. 100% of entry fees support spinal cord research. Marketing tools and promotional materials are available for organisers of local app runs. Taking part supports research into treatments for severed spinal cords; the event also includes merchandise sales and the option to join remotely, with all proceeds going to scientific research.

name: Botaniczna Piątka Olsztyn - edycja wiosenna 2026

The event takes place in the picturesque Warmia and Mazury Forest Arboretum, highlighting the scenic qualities of the course. The race is participant-friendly, and the organizers emphasize the beauty of the locations and promoting running among different groups. It is a great opportunity to combine sport with time in nature and earn a unique hyacinth-themed medal.

Picturesque, scenic woodland surroundings
Spring race featuring a unique hyacinth-themed medal

The race takes place in beautiful dendrological gardens, making it a unique experience for nature and sports enthusiasts.

There are four challenges to choose from: Lucyfer 21 km (3 loops), Boruta 14 km (2 loops), Rokita 7 km (1 loop), and Nordic Walking 7 km. This race is for those who value endurance, strength, and determination, with professional timekeeping and commemorative medals for participants.

Dynamic sections where survival matters more than speed

name: VIII Charytatywny Bieg Nadziei
location: Park Cegielnia, Żory, Śląskie Voivodeship, Poland

The event is open to everyone, regardless of athletic ability, and promotes physical activity combined with helping those in need.

name: XRUN Wyspowy Trail
description: Wyspowy Trail is a mountain trail race held in the Beskid Wyspowy, offering four distances: 50 km, 38 km, 22 km, and short races for children. The longest course crosses wild, forested terrain, including a route beneath Mogielica, the range’s highest peak, with beautiful views of the Tatras and the legendary climb up Modyń, where ropes help runners climb. The race takes place on 17 May 2026, with the finish at Limanowa Municipal Park and starts in Limanowa and nearby locations. Time limits are tailored to the course distances. It is a challenging and scenic adventure for mountain-running enthusiasts.
course_highlights: The course crosses wild, forested terrain in the Beskid Wyspowy
Views of the Tatras from the Mogielica area (1,170 m above sea level)
The legendary climb up Modyń, with ropes to help runners tackle the steep slope
additional: The race office and finish are located in Limanowa Municipal Park. The distances start at different locations: 50 km from the Wilczyce car park, 38 km from Rydz-Śmigły Pass in Słopnice, and 22 km from Zalesie. The time limits are 10h, 8h, and 6h, respectively. Age categories for the children’s races are for ages 3 to 15. Course maps and regulations are available on the website. Mountain courses, marked with tape and arrows; starts in Polrzeczki; online registration; regional character of the event.

name: Bieg Po Puszczy
location: Polana Sitowiec, Puszcza Niepołomicka, Niepołomice, Poland

Participants can choose from three running distances: a half marathon, the Forest 15K and the Forest 7K, and can also take part in the 40 km Gravel in the Forest cycling race. The course follows forest trails, gravel roads and asphalt, offering beautiful views and a chance to connect with nature. Every participant will receive a commemorative anniversary medal, and aid stations and professional medical support will be available along the course. The event is also an opportunity to spend time together as a family, with recreational cycling events for children.

Ekiden Junior for the youngest runners is also held as part of the event.

Start by the HP Park Poznań Hotel; finish by the grandstands and relay zone

The event ambassador is Dominika Stelmach, who also leads a special women’s team with athletic requirements. The event features team competition, the EKIDEN Junior race for children, charitable support, attractions, and an exciting atmosphere of sporting competition.

The race is part of the Kołobrzeska Odyssey series, promoting a healthy lifestyle and bringing the running community together. The time limit for completing the half marathon is 3 hours, and timing is electronic, using disposable chips.

Course marked every kilometre with vertical signs
Five refreshment stations along the course

The routes pass through scenic landscapes and feature technical elements such as climbs, sand and roots, as well as historic sites in the Municipality of Prostki, including the Border Pillar from 1545 and a former wooden Evangelical church from 1667. The start and finish are at the forest stadium in Prostki, providing a comfortable spot for spectators. The race is part of the season-long Kresowe Trail series, with overall and team classifications, and the option to take part in the DUAL competition combining running and cycling.

This is an endurance race where speed, strategy and perseverance all matter.

additional: There is no podium—only a throne for the winner. The event is for adults. The time limit for completing each loop is 1 hour. The rules and map are available to download on the website.
