It will take place on June 13, 2026, in Zagwiździe, on the grounds of the historic Ironworks complex. The event includes several categories: a 12 km run, a 3.5 km run, children’s races, and Nordic Walking. The race office will be open from 8:00 to 9:30, and timing will be electronic. This sporting event combines competition with a beautiful historic setting, encouraging physical activity and community engagement.

Electronic timing provides accurate results
additional: The race office is open from 8:00 to 9:30. Categories include a 12 km run, a 3.5 km run, children’s races, and Nordic Walking. The organizer is the Municipality of Murów. name: XIX Bieg Marszałka
description: The 19th Marshal’s Run is an annual road race held in Sulejówek, commemorating the traditions of the pre-war Sulejówek–Belweder marches. The main race, approximately 10 km long, takes place in June and commemorates Józef Piłsudski settling in Sulejówek. The event also includes accompanying races, including the Halina Zielińska Memorial over 3.6 km and races for children. The race has a patriotic and sporting character, with uniformed services and museum staff taking part. The start and finish are at 94 Paderewskiego Street, next to Willa Bzów.

Halina Zielińska Memorial over approximately 3.6 km
Traditional start and finish by Willa Bzów, 94 Paderewskiego Street
additional: The main race and the Halina Zielińska Memorial start at 10:20, the Little Kids’ Run at 10:30, and the Older Kids’ Run at 10:40. A flower-laying ceremony at the monument to Marshal Józef Piłsudski takes place at 9:50. Race packages can be officially and safely transferred to another participant. Uniformed services and museum staff also compete in separate categories. Registration and race-package collection take place at the Józef Piłsudski Museum, with registration also available by email. The event features various distances and forms of competition, including races for children and seniors.

name: XV Bieg Szlakiem Króla Zygmunta Starego
description: The 15th Run in the Footsteps of King Sigismund the Old is an annual race held in Kozienice, commemorating a historic route associated with King Sigismund the Old. The event takes place in the evening, with a start time of 18:00. Participants can use municipal parking near the amphitheatre.

Start and finish at the municipal amphitheatre, 31 Grodzieńska Street
Additional 5 km races and a 400 m race for children

description: Tatra Fest is a unique mountain festival held in Zakopane, bringing together a range of outdoor disciplines, including mountain running, climbing, cycling, trekking, and family activities. The event includes challenging races along Tatra trails, such as the 68 km Tatra Fest Bieg and the 22 km Tatra Fest Run, offering participants unforgettable experiences amid the Tatra Mountains’ scenic landscapes. The festival attracts both professionals and amateurs, promoting physical activity, contact with nature, and environmental responsibility. The organizers invite everyone to celebrate life and the mountain spirit together.
course_highlights: Tatra Fest Bieg 68 km: a skyrunning course with 5000 m of elevation gain, running above 2000 m above sea level, with exposed trails and fixed ropes

The Tatra Fest Run 22 km race package includes transport to the start. The finish in Zakopane’s Municipal Park offers food and drinks. The event includes various distances, including 68 km, 22 km, and 11 km, as well as vertical and family competitions. description: Dziki Groń is a challenging mountain course for Pieniny Ultra-Trail®, following hiking and courier-smuggling trails as well as routes across the mountain pastures of the Little Pieniny. The race offers scenic views of the Tatras and the Beskid Mountains, with the start and finish at Dietl Square in Szczawnica. It is intended for experienced mountain runners looking to take on demanding natural terrain. The event is part of the Pieniny Ultra-Trail mountain running festival, which promotes an active lifestyle and the Pieniny region.

Crosses the mountain pastures of the Little Pieniny

There are 5 aid stations on the course, including one at 12 km by the mountain shelter. Mandatory equipment is required in accordance with the regulations. The event promotes an active lifestyle and the Pieniny region. Registration opens in November 2025. Date: June 14, 2026. The course is approximately 64 km long. The event takes place in Szczawnica, and the route includes mountain trails and the pastures of the Little Pieniny.

The half-marathon course is flat and runs through the town streets over two laps, with numerous refreshment and hydration stations. The run promotes a healthy lifestyle, physical activity and integration within the local community. Free shorter-distance races for children, tailored to their age, are also planned. The race office and event base are located in the Manor Park by the Municipal Cultural and Recreation Centre in Haczów.

The event attracts both experienced ultramarathoners and trail-running enthusiasts who want to take on demanding terrain and enjoy the beauty of nature. The organizers provide full support at aid stations and specify the required equipment, ensuring participants’ safety and comfort.

description: The Warsaw Uprising Run is an annual running event held in Warsaw in remembrance of the Heroes of the Warsaw Uprising. The event attracts thousands of participants who take part in the 5 km and 10 km races, creating a unique, solemn atmosphere of patriotism and historical remembrance. The run uses staggered starts and takes place in the evening, further highlighting its distinctive character. The organizers also offer a virtual edition, allowing participants to take part from anywhere in the world.

name: Chudy Wawrzyniec
description: Chudy Wawrzyniec is a mountain ultramarathon held in the Żywiec Beskids, offering six distances from 3 km to 100 km. The event takes place on 8–9 August 2026, starting in Rajcza and finishing in Ujsoły. The courses are technically demanding, with significant elevation gain and beautiful views, and the 80 km race is the venue for the Polish Mountain Running Championships over the Ultra Distance. The organizers provide professional race organization and aid stations along the course, as well as the option to transfer a race entry.
course_highlights: Courses with significant elevation gain: 50 km (+2,525 m), 80 km (+3,825 m), 100 km (+5,115 m)
Technically demanding mountain trails with numerous ascents and descents
Start in Rajcza, finish in Ujsoły, with routes passing through Wielka Rycerzowa, Pilsko and other peaks
additional: The time limit for the 50/80/100 km distances is 16 hours. On the 100 km course, runners must reach the checkpoint at Trzy Kopce within a maximum of 11 h 30 min to continue. Aid stations are provided along the courses (3 on the 100 km, 2 on the 80 km, 1 on the 50 km), with no disposable cups. Race entries can be transferred to another participant from 1 April to 31 July. The time limit for finishing is 16 hours.

organizer: Stowarzyszenie Bieg Świętego Dominika w Ustroniu
description: The St. Dominic’s International Run is a prestigious annual running event held in Gdańsk since 1994 and an integral part of St. Dominic’s Fair. This unique sporting event attracts both recreational and professional runners, offering races over various distances in the picturesque city centre, on a course that loops around Neptune. The event promotes a healthy lifestyle and social integration, while creating an unforgettable atmosphere with thousands of spectators cheering and a rich programme of accompanying activities. It is valued by local authorities and sponsors, underscoring its stature and importance in Poland’s running calendar.
course_highlights: A 1,412 m course in central Gdańsk, looping around Neptune
A loop along Długi Targ, Powroźnicza, Kotwiczników and other streets
More than 25,000 spectators cheering along the course at each race
additional: The event includes four races under the slogan “Chase St. Dominic”, including a prologue open to all fair visitors, a race for people with disabilities, and classic women’s and men’s races over 5 km and 10 km. The course is a closed loop, allowing spectators to follow the competition closely. The event is accompanied by a rich programme of attractions, including partner stands, presentations, shows and concerts at St. Dominic’s Fair. A charity race over 10 km and 5 km, with entry fees donated to charitable causes, included in the USTRON GRAND PRIX.

description: The Bieg Kurierów Sądeckich is a historic mountain race held in the Beskid Sądecki Mountains, on a route from Rytro to the PTTK mountain shelter on Przehyba. The route is marked and covers a variety of surfaces: 15% asphalt, 5% gravel roads, and 80% forest trails, offering participants a chance to connect with nature on challenging terrain. The race commemorates couriers from World War II, and the course record is just under an hour. The organizer provides timekeeping, medical support, a commemorative medal, and a hot meal after the race.

The event is aimed mainly at experienced athletes, but amateurs can also test their skills on this extreme course. name: VIII Dycha nad Wisłą
description: The VIII Dycha nad Wisłą is an annual road race held in Tczew and is part of the IX Kociewie Running Grand Prix. The event attracts runners from various regions and offers a scenic route along the Vistula. It has a sporting and recreational character, promoting physical activity and community integration.
course_highlights: The route runs along scenic streets of Tczew beside the Vistula
The flat course profile is conducive to fast times
Organized as part of the Kociewie Running Grand Prix
additional: Registration is open, with a limit of 300 participants. Race packages include T-shirts. There are attractions and prizes, a riverside venue, and various registration options.

name: X Jubileuszowy Charytatywny Cross
description: The 10th Anniversary Charity Cross-Country Run and Nordic Walking event in Iwonicz-Zdrój is an annual sporting event held at Dietl Square in Iwonicz-Zdrój. The event combines a cross-country run and a Nordic walking march, promoting physical activity and a healthy lifestyle in this beautiful spa town. This anniversary edition attracts participants of different ages and skill levels. The organizers invite everyone to take part and emphasize the charitable nature of the event.
course_highlights: Cross-country run through the spa town of Iwonicz-Zdrój
Nordic walking march as an integral part of the event
Start and finish at Dietl Square, the town’s central point
additional: The event takes place on August 28–30, 2026, at Dietl Square in Iwonicz-Zdrój. It is organized by the Centre for Culture and Reading in Iwonicz-Zdrój. No information is available about entry fees, start times, or participant limits. The event also includes Nordic walking, training preparations, and online registration. The run is part of local social and cultural initiatives.

description: The 16th Baltic Sea Coast Marathon is an annual running event held in the picturesque towns of Jastarnia and Władysławowo. Participants can choose between the marathon and half-marathon distances, both running along the seashore and offering exceptional views and atmosphere. The event attracts runners from various age groups, including the K60+ and M65+ categories. The participant limit is 250, ensuring an intimate and friendly atmosphere.
course_highlights: The course runs along the shore of the Baltic Sea
Picturesque views of the sea and the coastal towns of Jastarnia and Władysławowo
Available distances: marathon (42 km) and half marathon (21 km)
additional: The participant limit is 250. The K60+ and M65+ age categories have reduced entry fees. Registration is open from 16 March to 26 August 2026. The fee on event day is higher. The start and finish are in the coastal towns of Jastarnia and Władysławowo. The participant limit is 250; registration opens on 16 March 2026 and includes information about dates and fees.

name: XVII Maraton Pieszo i Rowerem Dookoła Lubina
11 Bieg po Oddech
location: Zakopane, Tatra County, Lesser Poland Voivodeship, Poland

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: Dla dzieci i młodzieży do lat 17 włącznie. Pakiet z koszulką

tiers.label: tier_3
tiers.description: Dla dzieci i młodzieży do lat 17 włącznie. Pakiet bez koszulki

tiers.label: tier_4
tiers.description: Pakiet dla chorych na mukowiscydozę. Pakiet z koszulką

description: The 11th Bieg po Oddech is a charity 5 km run through the streets of Zakopane, taking place on 30 August 2026. The event supports people with cystic fibrosis, and every participant receives a T-shirt and a medal. After the run, a family picnic with games and contests is held. The run promotes physical activity as part of rehabilitation and support for people with the condition, as well as social integration.
course_highlights: A 5 km route through the picturesque streets of Zakopane
Start and finish in the City Park
The route is marked with vertical signs every 1 km
additional: Electronic timekeeping is provided by S-Time. After the run, there is refreshments and a family picnic with games and contests. The route, start and finish are in the City Park. The route is marked every 1 km. The virtual run of at least 5 km can be completed anywhere from 1 April to 30 September 2026. Participants can take part in the virtual run from April to September 2026, covering at least 5 km, or join the live event in Zakopane on 30 August 2026. Participants can expect race packs and a family charity picnic.

name: Jurajskie Mistrzostwa NA SKRAJU PRZEŁAJU
description: The Jurassic Championships ON THE EDGE OF CROSS-COUNTRY are challenging cross-country races held in picturesque Przewodziszowice near Żarki, in the Kraków-Częstochowa Upland. The routes wind through Jurassic hills, limestone outcrops, dense forests, winding paths, rocky climbs and open spaces with views of the Jurassic Landscape Park. The event offers a variety of distances, from short races for beginners and Nordic walkers to the demanding Trentaraton for experienced runners. It’s a great opportunity to compete and enjoy the beauty of nature.
course_highlights: Jurassic hills and limestone outcrops
Winding paths and rocky climbs
Views of the Jurassic Landscape Park
additional: The race office is open on 30 August 2026 from 8:00 to 10:00. Online registration is available until 24.08.2026; from 24.08.2026, registration is available only on race day at the race office. Children can participate for free. The event also includes Nordic walking over distances of 14 km and 7 km. Distances from 7 km to 30 km, races for children, on-site registration from 8:00, Jurassic terrain, races and walks, a sports and recreational event.

name: 47. Półmaraton Szczecin Bieg na 10 km
location: Plac Jasne Błonia im. Jana Pawła II, Szczecin, Poland
description: The 47th PKO Szczecin Half Marathon is an annual running event taking place on 30 August 2026 in Szczecin. Participants can choose between the half-marathon distance (21.0975 km) and a 10 km race, both following a single-loop route through the city streets. The start and finish are at Jan Paweł II Jasne Błonia Square. The course is certified by PZLA and marked every kilometre, and timing is electronic, using chips in the race bibs. The organisers offer wave starts and high-quality Ventus technical shirts in the extended race packages.
course_highlights: Single-loop route through the streets of Szczecin
Distance-choice point at 9.6 km on the route
PZLA-certified course, marked every kilometre
additional: Participants can choose a basic or extended package, with a Ventus technical shirt included in the extended package. Start and finish at Jan Paweł II Jasne Błonia Square. Participant limit: 6,000. Electronic timing using chips in the race bibs. Wave starts available. Race packages can be shipped by InPost courier, with the option to redirect them to a parcel locker. Distances: half marathon and 10 km race; location: Jasne Błonia, Szczecin; date: 30 August 2026, 09:00–13:00

name: IRONMAN 70.3 Poznan
location: Jezioro Kierskie, Poznań, Greater Poland Voivodeship, Poland
description: IRONMAN 70.3 Poznań is a prestigious triathlon held by historic Lake Kierskie, the site of Poland’s first triathlon in 1984. Athletes can expect calm, warm waters for the swim; a fast, flat bike course through picturesque villages and the western part of Poznań; and a run towards the city centre, finishing at the Poznań International Fairgrounds, a modern symbol of the city. This unique event combines sporting competition with local culture and modern infrastructure.
course_highlights: Swim in the calm, warm waters of Lake Kierskie, the site of Poland’s first triathlon
A flat, fast bike course through villages and the western part of Poznań
A run towards the city centre, finishing at the Poznań International Fairgrounds
additional: The race starts in a rolling-start format. The start and finish venues are Lake Kierskie and the Poznań International Fairgrounds. IRONKIDS will take place the day before, on August 29, 2026, with a start time of 11:00. Registration for the main race is sold out; notifications are available in case additional places open up. Participants can change their race date free of charge under the Flex90 offer. The event also includes activities such as the Night Run and IRONKIDS, and the participant limit is 1,500. Registration requires a credit card.

name: Kresowe Trail #10
description: Kresowe Trail is a series of small-scale trail races organized by the Kresowe Marathons Foundation, promoting a healthy lifestyle and physical activity in nature. The races take place on scenic routes in eastern Poland, with respect for nature and local communities. The events are intended for both beginners and experienced runners, and aim to build a running community based on passion, competition, and friendship. They are non-commercial and intimate, with a limited number of participants to ensure safety and high-quality organization.
course_highlights: Trail routes through scenic forests and hilly areas of eastern Poland
Respect for nature and local communities
Small-scale events with a limited number of participants
additional: The races are small-scale, with a limited number of participants. The organizer provides electronic timing, medical cover, aid stations along the course and at the finish, and commemorative medals. Participants can earn points toward the overall standings and titles of Finisher and Super Finisher by completing multiple races. The organizer encourages respect for the environment and asks participants not to litter on the routes. The event brings together the trail-running community, promotes outdoor activity, and supports the development of the local running scene. Registration takes place through an online platform, and the event is part of a series held at various locations.

name: Półmaraton Buski
organizer: Buski Ośrodek Sportu i Rekreacji w Busku-Zdroju

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Pierwsza tura zapisów potrwa do 31 maja

description: The Busko Half Marathon is an annual running event held in Busko-Zdrój. In 2026, it will take place on August 30. The race starts at 8:30 a.m. from the Municipal Stadium. The half-marathon route passes notable hotels and sanatoriums, the picturesque Spa Park, and charming promenades, giving the race a unique atmosphere. The time limit for covering the 21.0975 km distance is 3 hours and 30 minutes. The race is open to both experienced runners and amateurs.
course_highlights: The route passes notable hotels and sanatoriums in Busko-Zdrój
The race goes through picturesque Spa Park and charming promenades
A unique atmosphere and scenic surroundings along the route
additional: The time limit for completing the half marathon is 3 hours and 30 minutes. The route is established and popular, and this is the fourth year the race has been held on the same course. The event is organized by the Busko Sports and Recreation Centre and Athletics Busko-Zdrój Sports Club. GPX files of the route are available to download for Suunto and Garmin devices. Registration is open until May 31, 2026. Start time: 8:30 a.m. Time limit: 3 hours and 30 minutes. The route covers urban and park areas.

name: VII Maraton od Zmierzchu do Świtu
Leśna Piątka Odwrotnie
description: Leśna Piątka Odwrotnie is a cross-country race held in Koszalin on September 3, 2026. The course follows the usual route in the opposite direction, allowing participants to experience it anew. The event is open to runners, Nordic Walking enthusiasts, and mixed pairs. All participants receive medals at the finish, with trophies for the top finishers in various categories. The race is the season finale of Leśne Piątki and part of the Touru Biegów po Okolicy - TurBO, encouraging activity throughout the year.
course_highlights: Cross-country route in the forest of the Karnieszewice Forest District
Start and finish at the car park on Słupska Street in Koszalin
The route is run in the opposite direction, offering a chance to experience it anew
additional: Race numbers with chips can be collected at the race office on race day. Participants can compete in the running, Nordic Walking, and mixed-pair categories. The race is part of the Touru Biegów po Okolicy - TurBO, where the kilometres covered count, not pace. After the race, a photo gallery prepared by the A7 FILM team will be available. Participants can register online. The event also features photography attractions and is part of the Touru Biegów po Okolicy (TurBO).

name: Nocny Jelczański Bieg Towarzyski 3
description: Nocny Jelczański Bieg Towarzyski 3 is a night race covering 10 km, taking place on September 4, 2026, in Jelcz-Laskowice. It’s a great opportunity to test your fitness on a scenic course and prepare for autumn races. The organizers offer training plans tailored to different experience levels so that everyone can prepare for the race in the best possible way. The event is aimed at runners who enjoy the atmosphere of running at night and sporting competition.
course_highlights: 10 km distance
A night race in the scenic town of Jelcz-Laskowice
A course suited to an intermediate difficulty level
additional: The organizer offers training plans lasting 8 to 20 weeks, tailored to the runner’s VDOT level, as well as expert support. The event is promoted on the TreningBiegacza.pl platform, which enables race listing management and marketing collaboration. The event is part of local sports initiatives promoting outdoor activity and bringing the running community together.

name: RAWki na Surowo
location: Bieszczadzki Park Narodowy, Wetlina, Bieszczady, Poland
description: RAWki na Surowo is a mountain trail race held in the magical Bieszczady Mountains, taking runners across the scenic mountain meadows of Mała and Wielka Rawka. The 29 km course with +1550 m of elevation gain runs through Bieszczady National Park, requiring the race to be held without aid stations or course markings. The event is certified by ITRA and UTMB and is part of the MTrail Running Series. The start and finish are in Wetlina, and the race follows a self-supported format that underscores its rugged character.
course_highlights: A 29 km course with +1550 m of elevation gain across the mountain meadows of Mała and Wielka Rawka
A self-supported race with no aid stations or course markings
A route through Bieszczady National Park, with views towards the Polish-Ukrainian and Polish-Slovak borders
additional: The race starts at 08:00 from the ticket office by the green trail to Mała Rawka. The finish and race office are at Wetlina 36, at Arszenik - Jadło & Nalewki. The race office is open on 4 September from 18:00 to 21:00 and on 5 September from 06:30 to 07:30. The time limit for completing the course is 15:30. The start and finish locations are about 1,300 m apart. Participant parking is available in Wetlina, including by the green trail to Jawornik. There are no aid or water stations, so participants must be self-sufficient. The main distance is approximately 28.5 km, with access restricted due to park regulations. The event also includes online registration and electronic timing.

name: 60. Festiwal Chodu
location: Portowy region Gdańska, Gdańsk, Pomorskie, Poland
description: The 60th Walking Festival is a prestigious international sporting event held in the port region of Gdańsk on 5 September 2026. It brings together athletes of various ages and ability levels, with race-walking events over 10 km (women and men, including Open, U20 and U18 categories), 5 km and 3 km for younger participants, as well as the Polish Masters Championships over 5 km. The festival also includes the Polish U23 Championships over 10 km and accompanying events such as the “Walk with the Postman” Prologue and the Polish Post Office Defenders’ Run – Energa Cup. The organiser, LECHIA Gdańsk Athletics Club, promotes physical activity among people with disabilities, too, with wheelchair races and FrameRunning competitions.
course_highlights: Race walking over 10 km, 5 km and 3 km, with distances suited to different age categories
Polish Masters Championships over 5 km and Polish U23 Championships over 10 km
Accompanying events, including the “Walk with the Postman” Prologue and the Polish Post Office Defenders’ Run
additional: The festival promotes physical activity among people with disabilities through wheelchair races and FrameRunning competitions. It is organised by LECHIA Gdańsk Athletics Club and supported by the Ministry of Sport and Tourism. Events cover several distances, including 10 km, 5 km and 3 km, and online registration is available. The event promotes sporting activity among people of different ages and people with disabilities, with support from the Ministry of Sport and Tourism.

name: Chojnik Karkonoski Festiwal Biegowy
location: Sobieszów, Jelenia Góra, Lower Silesian Voivodeship, Poland

tiers.label: tier_4
tiers.description: 300 zł – w płacone 1 sierpnia – 5 września 2026 r.

description: The Chojnik Karkonoski Running Festival is a mountain running event held in Sobieszów, in the heart of the Karkonosze Mountains. The festival offers a variety of distances, from a family educational run to a demanding 102 km ultramarathon with over 5,000 m of elevation gain. The routes follow scenic, rocky trails in Karkonosze National Park, offering unique views and challenges for runners of varying abilities. The event fosters a sense of community and promotes running as a team sport, as well as nature education.
course_highlights: Routes pass through Karkonosze National Park, with rocky descents and demanding climbs
102 km ultramarathon with over 5,110 m of elevation gain and a 20-hour time limit
Start and finish by Chojnik Castle in Sobieszów, with scenic mountain views
additional: Race starts take place from 2:00 (Ultra Chojnik) to 10:30 (Educational Run). The participant limit for Ultra Chojnik is 100, and for the Chojnik Marathon it is 325. Mandatory equipment for the ultra includes, among other things, a headlamp, a phone with roaming, an NRC emergency blanket, and a course map. Aid stations and drop bags are available along the route. The Educational Run features educational stops and nature-related questions. Mountain terrain, a limit of 325 participants, mandatory equipment required, aid stations along the route, 9-hour time limit.

name: Olkuski Bieg Uliczny
location: Stadion przy ul. 29 Listopada 12c, Olkusz, Poland
description: The Olkusz Street Run VII Silver Ten is an annual running event organized by the Olkuszbiega Association, the Olkusz City and Municipal Office, and the Municipal Sports and Recreation Centre in Olkusz. The main 10 km race consists of two 5 km loops, with chip timing and route markers every kilometre. The course runs along asphalt and partially cobbled streets; the start and finish are at the Market Square in Olkusz. The event promotes an active lifestyle and running as a recreational activity for all age groups.
course_highlights: The 10 km course consists of two 5 km loops
Asphalt and partially cobbled surfaces
Route markers every 1 km and a split time at 5 km
additional: The time limit to finish the race is 90 minutes. There is a refreshment station at approximately 6 km. The participant limit is 300. Verification and race-pack collection take place on 6 and 7 September. Chip timing is used, with the chip attached to the shoe. Participants under 18 must have written parental consent. The participant limit is 300, and the time limit for completing the course is 90 minutes. Online registration is available. The entry fee is non-refundable; it may be transferred until 26.08.2024.

name: Półmaraton Praski
description: The Praski Half Marathon is an annual running event held in Warsaw, attracting both recreational and experienced runners. The half-marathon course passes through the scenic and historic parts of Praga, offering participants exceptional views and atmosphere. The event takes place at night, giving it a unique character and appeal. The organizers provide professional support, timekeeping, and race packs that include an official T-shirt.
course_highlights: The course passes through the historic Praga district of Warsaw
The race takes place in the evening, giving the event a nighttime character
Scenic views and the unique atmosphere of a night half marathon
additional: Official race T-shirt for participants. Electronic timekeeping. The event is held at night, with the start at 20:00. Race packs with a race bib and chip are available. The course is certified and secured. Participants can also take part in the 5 km race, the Praska 5k Run. The event also includes results and details about the course and regulations. The races are open to a wide range of participants, and the event is growing in popularity among runners from Warsaw and the surrounding area.

name: XLVI Usedom Marathon
description: The XLVI International Usedom Marathon is a unique running event that crosses two countries along Europe’s longest seaside promenade. The 42 km course connects Świnoujście in Poland with Wolgast in Germany, passing through historic seaside resorts and scenic woodland. Runners can enjoy varied surfaces and beautiful views of the Baltic Sea, as well as the unique atmosphere of Usedom Island.
course_highlights: The route follows Europe’s longest seaside promenade
Passes through the historic seaside resorts of Ahlbeck, Heringsdorf and Bansin
Varied surfaces: asphalt, cobblestones and forest trails
additional: Transport to the marathon start is provided by the organizer’s buses, with a stop near the race office at 7:15. Boarding is available at various points on Usedom Island. Baggage transport to the stadium in Wolgast is provided. Time limit: runners must pass Kölpinsee (km 21.8) within 2:30 h and Zinnowitz (km 30) within 3:30 h; otherwise, they will be withdrawn from the course. After these time limits, the course will not be supported and no refreshment stations will be available. Start in Świnoujście, finish in Wolgast, bus transfer available, registration until 30 August 2026. The routes include urban, forest and coastal sections.

name: I Mistrzostwa Śląska Osób z Niepełnosprawnościami
V Bieg Pamięci Ofiar Bombardowania Węzła Kolejowego
XIV Grand Prix Nordic Walking Nowa Wieś Lęborska
14 Tyski Półmaraton
location: Stadion Lekkoatletyczny w Tychach, Tychy, Silesian Voivodeship, Poland
description: The 14th Tychy Half Marathon is a PZLA-certified half-marathon (21.0975 km) run through the streets of Tychy and around Paprocany Lake. The start, finish and race village are located at the Tychy Athletics Stadium. The event promotes an active lifestyle and the city’s sporting atmosphere, and also offers numerous accompanying attractions, such as children’s races, massages and sports demonstrations. The course was modified in 2022 to reduce the number of uphill sections, making it more participant-friendly. The race is held under the honorary patronage of the Mayor of Tychy and has been growing in popularity since 2012.
course_highlights: Street course and route around Paprocany Lake (asphalt, paving stones and paved path)
Vertical signs mark every kilometre
Finish at the Tychy Athletics Stadium
additional: The time limit is 3 hours. Electronic timing uses a chip in the race bib, with net-time classification. Water stations are available along the course. The race office and race-pack collection will be available on 4–5 September 2026 at Gemini Park Tychy, and on race day from 6:30 to 8:30 at the stadium. The race pack includes a chip bib, technical shirt (if the entry fee is paid by 2 August), medal, hot post-race meal, drinks, medical support and course safety measures. Children’s races take place before and after the main race. The event will take place in an urban setting, with race offices at Gemini Park Tychy and the Athletics Stadium. The programme also includes races for the youngest participants.

name: 26 Eco Półmaraton Wałbrzych
description: The 26th Toyota Eko Półmaraton Wałbrzych is one of the most important running events in the region and across the country, attracting runners from all over Poland. Following last year’s organisational success and record attendance, the event once again confirms its strong position on Poland’s sporting map. Participants rated the half-marathon course very highly, and the unique atmosphere created by the supporters of Wałbrzych gives the event its distinctive character. We warmly invite you to take part and cheer on the runners.
course_highlights: New, highly rated half-marathon course
Unique atmosphere thanks to Wałbrzych’s supporters
An event with an established place on Poland’s sporting map
additional: On 24.08.2025, there will be traffic disruptions and special transport for participants and supporters. A Racebook is available—a practical guide with essential information before the start. In addition to the half-marathon, accompanying races and junior races are also organised. Registration opens on 27 January 2026; the event includes a half-marathon, 10 km races and children’s races. Participants can choose from different race packages and enjoy attractions at the Old Mine.

name: 44 Międzynarodowy Otwarty Bieg Przełajowy o Puchar Leśny pamięci Tomasza Hopfera
description: Join the 44th International Open Cross-Country Race for the Forest Cup in memory of Tomasz Hopfer, taking place on 6 September 2026 in Obliwice. The main race course is 6.4 km long and consists of two 3.2 km loops, with the start and finish in the same place. The event has a unique sporting atmosphere, combining competition with recreation for the whole family amid nature. The race commemorates Tomasz Hopfer, a legend of Polish sports journalism and an athlete, and promotes a healthy lifestyle and physical activity in the local community.
course_highlights: Main race course: two 3.2 km loops
Start and finish at the same point
Forest and natural surroundings in Obliwice
additional: Race schedule for 6 September 2026: ceremonial opening at 11:00; races for children and young people over 600 m and 1.609 km; main race start at 13:20 over 6.4 km; mayors’ and VIP race at 14:00; International Mile in memory of Piotr Gładki at 17:00; and the Ecological Feast at 17:30. Around 300 athletes are expected to take part in the main race. The top athletes in the main race qualify for the International Mile. Forest terrain, online registration, accompanying events, sports memorial.

name: 64 Bieg Westerplatte
description: The 64th Westerplatte Run is Poland’s oldest continuously held 10-kilometre road race, taking place in Gdańsk. The race starts at the historic site where World War II began, giving the event a unique character and an atmosphere of reflection on sacrifice and peace. The course is certified and marked at every kilometre, and the finish is at Polsat Plus Arena Gdańsk, providing an added attraction for participants. The event draws up to 5,000 runners and is both a sporting challenge and a tribute to the Defenders of the Coast in 1939.
course_highlights: Certified course marked every 1 km
An opportunity to run through the Tunnel under the Dead Vistula, which is normally closed to pedestrian traffic
Finish at Polsat Plus Arena Gdańsk, a modern football stadium
additional: Race bib collection at Polsat Plus Arena Gdańsk on 6–7 September 2026. Water station on the course at approximately 6 km. Participant limit: 5,000. Free buses will take runners to the start on race day. Bag drop available with a race bib sticker. No showers. The awards ceremony will take place at the finish at approximately 11:45. Cash prizes and trophies for the winners in the OPEN and age-group categories. Registration runs from 2026-03-02 to 2026-08-20, with a limit of 4,900 participants. Official T-shirts can be purchased at the Expo. The event includes race-pack collection, the Expo, transport, the start, and the awards ceremony at Westerplatte.

name: Bieg KoBBiet
location: Stadion Miejski, Bielsko-Biała, Silesian Voivodeship, Poland
description: KoBBiet Run is an annual race held in Bielsko-Biała. In 2026, it will take place on September 6 at the Municipal Stadium. The event is dedicated to the memory of Ewa Szymanek-Płaska, Head of the Education and Sport Department at Bielsko-Biała City Hall. This year’s race supports children on the autism spectrum, and registration opens on April 10, 2026, at 10:00. The race is held under the honorary patronage of Bielsko-Biała Mayor Jarosław Klimaszewski.
course_highlights: The route runs through the streets of central Bielsko-Biała
Start at the Municipal Stadium, finish at Wojska Polskiego Square
5 km distance with attractions at the finish
additional: The event supports children on the autism spectrum. Registration is available at datasport.pl. The race is dedicated to women, and commemorative medals and attractions await at the finish.

name: Szybka Piątka Sokoła
description: Szybka Piątka Sokoła is a 5 km race held in Bukownica, Mazowieckie. It’s a great opportunity for runners of all levels to test their fitness on an easy asphalt course. The organizers encourage participants to prepare using training plans tailored to their individual level, with support from experts. The event has a friendly, motivating atmosphere and is ideal for anyone looking to improve their fitness and enjoy running.
course_highlights: 5 km course
Easy asphalt surface
Scenic surroundings of Bukownica
additional: Training plans of 8 to 20 weeks are available, tailored to runners’ VDOT levels and accompanied by instructions and expert support. Training preparation is available to participants, and the event promotes physical activity and a healthy lifestyle in the local community.

name: XIV Panewnicki Bieg Dzika (9)
organizer: AWF Katowice, KS AZS AWF Katowice

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: dzieci i młodzież do lat 18 – w wysokości 20 zł przelewem na konto

tiers.label: tier_3
tiers.description: pozostałe osoby – w wysokości 45 zł przelewem na konto

tiers.label: tier_5
tiers.description: małżeństwa – w wysokości 80 zł przelewem na konto

description: Panewnicki Bieg Dzika is a recreational running and Nordic walking event held in the scenic Panewniki forests in Katowice. The event aims to promote an active, healthy lifestyle and the beauty of the local natural environment. The course is a loop of approximately 4.9 km, which participants can complete up to four times, with a time limit of 3 hours. The event is open to both recreational participants and athletes affiliated with sports clubs. Participants can also learn about appropriate conduct in the forest.
course_highlights: A course of approximately 4.9 km through the Panewniki forest
The loop is marked every 1 km
The course can be completed up to 4 times
additional: The time limit for completing the running and Nordic walking course is 3 hours. Participants can purchase a package of entries for the entire year 2026. People born in 1950 or earlier are exempt from the entry fee. Entry fees are non-refundable, but can be transferred to a later event after notifying the organizer. The event includes training preparation and information about training plans, making it appealing to runners of different experience levels.

name: XVIII Bieg Koguta

The event is organized by the Oławska Grupa Biegowa in cooperation with local institutions, and participants can expect professional timing. The race office will be open both the day before the race and on race day, making it easier to collect race packs. The race is open to runners of different ability levels.

Professional electronic timing
Support from local institutions and partners, including the “Termy Jakuba” Municipal Swimming Pools
additional: The race office is open on September 5 from 16:00 to 20:00 and on September 6 from 07:00 to 09:15. Participants must accept the race regulations and consents related to the processing of personal data. A third party may collect a race pack upon submission of the appropriate consent. The race office is located at the venue the day before the race. Online registration is available. Participant limit: 891.

The courses pass through rocky labyrinths, technical trails and beautiful rock formations such as Szczeliniec Wielki and Błędne Skały. The event attracts both beginners and experienced ultramarathon runners, offering a variety of distances and a special atmosphere close to nature. Radków is an ideal place for a sporting adventure and recovery amid nature.

Courses passing near Szczeliniec Wielki and Błędne Skały
Radków Reservoir nearby as a place to recover

name: 10. PKO Bieg Charytatywny
description: The 10th PKO Charity Run is a nationwide initiative that combines the excitement of sport with tangible support for an important social cause: the mental health of children and young people. The event will take place across Poland on September 12, 2026, encouraging participants to run together and take action for their communities. Every lap, kilometre and minute on the course matters, highlighting the spirit of community and helping others. This anniversary edition invites runners to take part and show their support.
course_highlights: Multiple locations across Poland, including Gdańsk, Ruda Śląska, Łomża, Krosno and Stalowa Wola
Virtual run option using an app
Charity relay races and runs for children and adults
additional: The event takes place across Poland, combining physical activity with a charitable cause supporting the mental health of children and young people. The PKO Charity Run is an initiative where it is not just the result that matters, but above all, acting together and supporting the community. The event supports the mental health of children and young people, includes relay races and fundraising for therapy, participation in many cities across Poland, and a virtual participation option.

name: Bieg 7 Dolin
location: Piwniczna-Zdrój, Nowy Sącz County, Lesser Poland Voivodeship, Poland
description: Bieg 7 Dolin is a 100 km mountain ultramarathon held in the scenic Sądecki Beskid Mountains, starting and finishing in Piwniczna-Zdrój. The course follows demanding mountain trails with significant elevation gain, offering participants exceptional views and a chance to connect with nature. The race is part of the Running Festival, which combines sporting competition with promoting the region and an active lifestyle. The time limit is 19 hours, and there are aid stations and drop-bag points along the course. It is a challenge for experienced mountain runners looking to take on demanding but beautiful terrain.
course_highlights: +3,740 m / -3,740 m elevation change over the 100 km course
6 aid stations and 3 drop-bag points along the course
The route follows trails in the Sądecki Beskid Mountains, with views of the mountains and the Poprad Valley
additional: The time limit to finish the race is 19 hours (until 21:00). Intermediate cutoffs: Rytro (36 km) — 7 hours (until 09:00); Krynica (62 km) — 12 hours (until 14:00); Wierchomla (89 km) — 17 hours (until 19:00). Recommended technical gear includes a reusable cup or bottle, a running backpack or belt, an emergency blanket, a headlamp, reflective gear, health insurance, a whistle, hand sanitizer, and a working phone with an ICE number written on the back of the race bib. The event features several distances, including 100 km, 42 km, 61 km, 23 km and 11 km, as well as accompanying attractions such as festivals and an expo. The races take place in early September 2026.

description: The 5th edition of the “Aktywna Piątka” race will take place on September 12, 2026, in Frydek, in the Miedźna Municipality. It is a fast road race on a route exactly 5 km long, certified by the Polish Athletics Association (PZLA), starting at 11:00. The event will also host the Silesian Voivodeship 5 km Championships, and the participant limit is 600. The accompanying Family Run is for children and teenagers up to 15 years old and features three distances.
course_highlights: Fast 5 km route certified by the PZLA
Asphalt course, marked every 1 km
Water station and cooling mist arches along the route
additional: The participant limit for the main race is 600. The first five women and men in the OPEN classification will be awarded. The race starts at 189C Modowa Street. The accompanying Family Run is for children and teenagers up to 15 years old, with three distances: 800 m for ages 10–15 and shorter distances for younger age groups. The commemorative medal is awarded only to the registered main participant in the Family Run. The limit for paid entries is 400. Running with a dog, wheelchair, or stroller is not permitted.

name: XVII Grand Prix Mysłowic
description: The Grand Prix Truchtacza in Mysłowice is a series of races organised by the Truchtacz Mysłowice Association, promoting a healthy, active lifestyle and bringing runners together from different regions. The event is open to everyone, regardless of age or experience, and participants can compete in running, Nordic walking and canicross. The races take place on forest and urban routes, creating a welcoming atmosphere of sporting competition and community. The Grand Prix is a tradition and a passion that has brought runners together for many years.
course_highlights: Forest routes near Bolina
A range of events: running, Nordic walking and canicross
Participants from many cities and sports clubs in the Silesian and Lesser Poland Voivodeships
additional: Registration for the Grand Prix series is available only at the Race Office on race day. Participation in Grand Prix events is free of charge. Both runners and Nordic walking and canicross participants take part. Competitors come from various cities and sports clubs, and women make up more than 27% of participants. The event includes various distances and seasonal races, promoting a healthy lifestyle and physical activity in the local community.

A road race in the center of Złotów
Organized at the Municipal Stadium and on nearby streets

name: Poznań Track Day 2026
location: Tor Poznań, Poznań, Greater Poland Voivodeship, Poland
description: Tor Poznań Track Day is a series of exciting motorsport events held at the race track in Poznań. Participants have the opportunity to compete, train, and take part in qualifying rounds held throughout the 2026 season. The event is aimed at motorsport enthusiasts and also offers car rentals and one-to-one instruction with instructors. It is a great opportunity to experience the thrill of motorsport and improve your skills on a professional track.
course_highlights: Race track in Poznań with professional facilities
Opportunity to take part in various rounds and qualifying sessions during the 2026 season
Training sessions and one-to-one instruction with instructors
additional: Cars can be rented for track use, for yourself or as a gift. The entry package includes participation by a team member, the option to co-drive (age >17), full catering, individual lap-time measurement, and the option of instruction with an instructor. Participation payments must include the correct payment reference to confirm entry. Multiple rounds include training sessions, qualifying, and night races, with a focus on sporty driving and the excitement of the track.

name: XI Bieg Nadziei oraz VII Mistrzostwa Wielkopolski Prawników
location: Środa Wielkopolska, Greater Poland Voivodeship, Poland
description: The 11th Run of Hope and the 7th Greater Poland Lawyers’ Championships are a charity run organized in Środa Wielkopolska to support the work of the Piotr Hospice. The event combines sporting competition with an important social cause, engaging the local community and the legal profession. It is an established tradition that promotes physical activity and solidarity.
course_highlights: Start and finish at the Old Market Square in Środa Wielkopolska
Charity run supporting the hospice
Various distances and activities, including children’s races and Nordic walking
additional: The run is a charity event supporting the Piotr Hospice. Registration opens on March 1, 2026. The website has no details about the course, start times, or fees. The event is scheduled for September 13, 2026, and includes various running and activity options; participation supports the work of the Piotr Hospice.

name: XRUN - Vistula Trail
location: Wisła, Cieszyn County, Silesian Voivodeship, Poland
description: Vistula Trail is a mountain trail race held in Wisła, offering a range of distances from short routes for children to challenging mountain courses. Runners can enjoy scenic views of the Beskids, starting in the center of Wisła or on the Czech side in Třinec. The routes pass notable locations such as Soszów Wielki, Soszów Mountain Hut and Czantoria, combining an international adventure with the character of the Beskids. This event is for mountain-running enthusiasts who value variety and beautiful natural landscapes.
course_highlights: Start in the heart of Wisła at Skolnity Ski & Bike Park
The route passes Soszów Wielki, Soszów Mountain Hut and Czantoria
Scenic descents along the green trail to the center of Wisła and Kopczyński Park
additional: Time limits: 35 km – 9h, 24 km – 7h, 15 km – 4h. Start times vary: 35 km at 07:00, 24 km at 08:00, 15 km at 09:30. Age categories for children aged 3 to 15 on the short distances. Start and finish in Wisła, with transport to the start of the Classic Trail distance from Třinec. The event offers various distances divided into age categories, organized transport for some routes, marked trails and a children’s category. The start is in a scenic area, with the opportunity to enjoy mountain landscapes.

name: 16 Bieg Częstochowski
description: The 16th Częstochowa Run is a road race taking place on September 13, 2026, in the center of Częstochowa. The 10 km course follows the city’s prominent avenues, including the area around Jasna Góra, giving the race a distinctive prestige. The course is officially certified, attracting runners aiming for a fast pace and personal bests. It is an excellent opportunity for sporting competition in picturesque urban surroundings.
course_highlights: 10 km course through the center of Częstochowa
Route passes near Jasna Góra
Officially certified course suited to fast running
additional: Registration takes place at the Sports Hall of IV High School; the fee is payable in cash. The event also includes training sessions and information from sponsors.

The course follows scenic trails and hills, offering participants varied terrain, including forest paths, rocky sections, and steep climbs. The race is suitable for both experienced runners and beginners who want to embrace the spirit of adventure and enjoy the fresh air. After the race, participants can look forward to commemorative medals, prizes, and a range of attractions, including activities for children. The event takes place in a friendly, sporty atmosphere.
course_highlights: A course along scenic trails and hills in Ojców National Park
Varied terrain: forest paths, rocky sections, and steep climbs
Stunning views of the surrounding area
additional: Available distances: Bieg po Pstrąga Ojcowskiego (8 km), with team rankings and a prize for the best resident of the Skała municipality, and Bieg Szlakiem Skał i Dolin (15 km), with a similar ranking. Children’s races are available over 100 m (ages 2–5, no ranking), 800 m (ages 10–11), and 1,300 m (ages 12–15). After the race, activities for younger children include inflatable castles, entertainers, and prize competitions. The course follows scenic trails and hills, with varied terrain ranging from forest paths to rocky sections and steep climbs. The event offers races at various distances, including children’s races, and GPX files are available to download. Race packs can be collected on 19–20.09.2025.

description: The Northern Running Festival is a unique running event taking place on 13 September 2026 on the Hel Peninsula, bringing together the tradition of the Northern Marathon and the Marathon Relays under one name. The course passes through the scenic locations of Hel, Jastarnia and Rozewie, along Puck Bay, with sea views and four lighthouses giving the race its unique character. The event offers a range of distances for runners of all ability levels, from the marathon and relays to the half marathon, 10 km and 5 km, as well as a children’s race, the Little Lighthouse Keeper Run. It’s not just a sporting event, but also a journey through the coast’s beautiful spots and a chance to connect with nature.

There are four lighthouses along the course: in Hel, Jastarnia and two in Rozewie
The course passes through some of the most beautiful spots on the Hel Peninsula and the coast

The Little Lighthouse Keeper Run is for children and young people up to 14 years old. The course is available to download in .GPX, .KML and .TCX formats; coastal and seaside terrain; the event includes various distances and competitions for adults and children.

The races take place on scenic routes in the Kozienice Forest near Jedlnia-Letnisko, giving participants the opportunity to compete in the marathon, half marathon, and other accompanying races. The marathon promotes a healthy lifestyle and sobriety, while also bringing the local running community together. It is a well-established event that attracts both amateur and experienced runners.

description: Żyrardów w Biegu is an annual running event organized by the Żyrardów Cycling Association, taking place on September 13, 2026, by the Żyrardów Reservoir. Participants can choose between two distances: 10 km and 5 km. Both routes go around the reservoir, with multiple laps and a finish at the reservoir grounds. The race promotes physical activity, community spirit and a welcoming sporting atmosphere, while also helping promote the city of Żyrardów and the Mazovia region. The event is open to adults, and athletes using active wheelchairs may also compete in the 10 km race.

4 laps for the 10 km distance; 2 laps for the 5 km distance
Start and finish by the Żyrardów Reservoir, 17 Ziołowa Street
additional: Online registration is available until September 10, 2026. After that date, registration is available only at the race office until 9:00 a.m. on race day. Each participant collects a race number with a chip at the race office. Athletes using active wheelchairs may compete in the 10 km race. The event base, start, finish and parking are by the Żyrardów Reservoir, 17 Ziołowa Street. Distances: 10 km and 5 km; online registration; a 100-minute time limit for the main race; wheelchair athletes may participate; the swimming area is open during the event weekend.

Maraton 3 Jezior / Three Lakes Marathon
location: Międzybrodzie Bialskie, Żywiec County, Silesian Voivodeship, Poland
description: The 3 Lakes Marathon is a mountain running festival held in the picturesque Beskid Mały region, in the Soła River valley. The main event is an ultramarathon of approximately 43 km with around 2,485 m of elevation gain, traversing the highest parts of the Beskid Mały mountains and offering beautiful views of three lakes and the surrounding mountains. The course combines demanding climbs with technical descents, giving participants the chance to experience both the region’s wild nature and its historic sites. The event takes place during the beautiful transition from summer to autumn, adding to the charm of the course and its surroundings.
course_highlights: Ultramarathon course of approximately 43 km with +/- 2,485 m of elevation change
Views of three lakes: Międzybrodzkie, Tresna, and the surrounding area
Technically demanding climbs and descents, including a steep climb to Magurka and the summit of Czupel
additional: Start and finish: the race starts at 8:00 in Międzybrodzie Bialskie and finishes at the stadium in Porąbka. Course time limit: 10h30min. The course passes through varied terrain, including forests, meadows, and a suspension bridge over the Soła. There are refreshment points along the course and a spectator zone in Czernichów. The course is technically demanding, with significant elevation gain. Other distances and accompanying races are also available as part of the festival. The event features a range of distances, a festival atmosphere, electronic timing, and courses through lakes and mountains, offering an unforgettable experience.

name: 23 Przejście Dookoła Kotliny Jeleniogórs...
location: Jelenia Góra, Lower Silesian Voivodeship, Poland
description: The Walk Around the Jelenia Góra Valley is one of Poland’s best-known long-distance hiking events, held since 2004. Participants cover a route of approximately 140 km around the Jelenia Góra Valley, crossing the Karkonosze, Rudawy Janowickie, Kaczawskie Mountains, and Izera Mountains. The event commemorates GOPR rescuers. The entry fee includes race materials, a souvenir, a hot meal, and a certificate. The route is demanding, with approximately 5,500 m of elevation gain, and participants have 48 hours to complete it.
course_highlights: A long route of approximately 140 km around the Jelenia Góra Valley
Approximately 5,500 m of total elevation gain
Crosses the Karkonosze, Rudawy Janowickie, Kaczawskie Mountains, and Izera Mountains
additional: There is no timekeeping or ranking. The entry fee includes race materials (a race number and route map), a logo souvenir (T-shirt), a hot meal and drinks at the refreshment point, water at selected checkpoints, a certificate, photography, a prize draw, and GOPR safety support. Long distance, mountain terrain, difficult weather conditions, and a memorial honoring GOPR rescuers.

name: 3 Backyard Ultra Zagłębie
description: Backyard Ultra Zagłębie is a unique ultramarathon run on a 6.706 km loop around Pogoria 3 Lake in Dąbrowa Górnicza. Runners start every hour, and the last person to finish each lap continues running until only one winner remains. The course combines a variety of surfaces—asphalt, dirt and forest trails, and a beach section—requiring both endurance and technical precision. The event is the final of the Polish Backyard Ultra League and attracts fans of extreme challenges from across Poland.
course_highlights: A 6.706 km loop around Pogoria 3 Lake
A mix of surfaces: 60% dirt and forest trails, 40% asphalt, paving stones, and concrete
A beach section of approximately 250–300 metres near the pier, plus steps at the finish
additional: Each lap starts exactly on the hour. Runners must be at the starting line within 3 minutes of the start of the lap or they are eliminated. The event village is located at the Summer and Water Sports Centre. The organizer reserves the right to adjust the course for weather or safety reasons. All runners except the winner receive a DNF (Did Not Finish) designation as a symbol of perseverance. Participant limit: 140; start time: 12:00; location: Dąbrowa Górnicza; ultramarathon format with hourly laps

name: 17. PKO Bytomski Półmaraton
organizer: Klub MKS MOSM Bytom, Ośrodek Sportu i Rekreacji w Bytomiu, Centrum Handlowe Plejada
description: The 17th PKO Bytom Half Marathon is an event promoting a healthy lifestyle and bringing together the local community of Bytom and the surrounding area. The race takes place on a certified, fully asphalt 21.097 km course consisting of a single loop. The start and finish are located at G City Plejada Shopping Centre in Bytom. Participants can expect refreshment and water stations, as well as pacemakers. After the race, they can personalize their medal by having their result engraved.
course_highlights: A certified PZLA half-marathon course, one loop and 21.097 km long
100% asphalt surface, with markings every 1 km
Refreshment and water stations along the course; 3-hour time limit
additional: After the race, participants can personalize their medal with their result engraved (cost: 25 zł). Pacemakers wearing balloons and special shirts will be on the course. The half-marathon time limit is 3 hours. After that, runners must stop and travel to the finish in a minibus marked KONIEC PÓŁMARATONU. A group warm-up is scheduled for 9:45. An activity zone is available for children. The event attracts over 1,200 participants each year and offers personalized medals, a 3-hour time limit, and activities for children. Registration is available online and at the race office.

name: PKO Wieczorny Półmaraton Łódź
description: The PKO Łódź Evening Half Marathon is a new, atmospheric running event held in the centre of Łódź. The start and finish are located at the revitalised EC1 combined heat and power plant, which is now a cultural and science centre. The 21.097 km course passes through the city’s best-known landmarks, bringing together its industrial history and modern character. This is a race where it’s not just the result that matters, but also the unique atmosphere and energy of the city.
course_highlights: Start and finish at the revitalised EC1 combined heat and power plant
The course passes through Łódź’s best-known landmarks
An evening road race in the city centre
additional: The participant limit is 5,000. The race pack includes a commemorative drawstring backpack, and everyone who finishes the race receives a medal. An official SMMASH technical shirt is available to purchase. Discounts are available to PKO Bank Polski customers paying online. Registration opened one week before the event. The course includes key locations in Łódź.

name: 44 Strzeliński Rogaining
location: Wzgórza Strzelińskie, Strzelin, Lower Silesian Voivodeship, Poland
organizer: Polskie Towarzystwo Turystyczno-Krajoznawcze Oddział Ziemi Strzelińskiej
description: Strzeliński Rogaining is an orienteering foot rally organized by the Polish Tourist and Sightseeing Society, Strzelin Land Branch, since 1996. Teams of 2–5 plan their own route, aiming to visit as many checkpoints as possible within the allotted time. The checkpoints have different point values, so success calls for both navigation skills and strategy. The event is open to participants of different ages and ability levels, making it an appealing activity for enthusiasts and families alike. It takes place in the scenic Strzelin Hills, offering a chance to enjoy nature and spend time actively outdoors.
course_highlights: The varied checkpoints of the Strzelin Hills
A route of any chosen length, from approximately 5 km to 70 km, planned by each team
Foot navigation using a map and compass
additional: Teams of 2–5 plan their route independently and may change it during the competition. Checkpoints have different point values depending on how difficult they are to find. The competition is open to everyone, regardless of age or gender, and results are divided into age and gender categories. Routes range from 6 to 70 km, with the option to register and plan a route before the start. The event takes place in the Strzelin Hills, among forests and varied terrain.

name: Gontyniec Celtic Trail
location: Gontyniec, Chodzież, Greater Poland Voivodeship, Poland
description: Gontyniec Celtic Trail is a unique reverse-format race, lasting 6 or 12 hours on loops of approximately 10 km through the picturesque Gontyniec Massif. Competitors cover the greatest distance they can, with well-stocked aid stations available after every loop. The course offers changing scenery at different times of day, with beautiful views of the Noteć Valley and unique natural and cultural attractions, such as beehives shaped like ancient gods. It is a unique experience for runners seeking a challenge and unforgettable impressions.
course_highlights: Non-stop race on loops of approximately 10 km
Aid station for competitors after every loop
Views of the Noteć Valley and unique figurative beehives along the course

The race is open to mass participation, with starting corrals assigned according to declared finish time, and participants can also enter 4-person relay teams. The organizers provide professional timekeeping, medical support, refreshments and water along the course. The event promotes physical activity and a healthy lifestyle, and helps raise the profile of Gdańsk in Poland and abroad.

description: The 49th Lechitów Half Marathon is Poland’s oldest half marathon, held continuously since 1978. The 21.0975 km race route runs from the Small Open-Air Museum in Ostrów Lednicki to the finish at Saint Adalbert’s Square in Gniezno, recalling the historic journey of Otto III. The race attracts thousands of runners every year and is part of the Polish Half Marathon Crown and the Greater Poland Half Marathon Grand Prix. The organizers provide professional race services, timing and course safety, while participants receive a race pack with a medal and a recovery meal.
course_highlights: Start at the Small Open-Air Museum in Ostrów Lednicki; finish at Saint Adalbert’s Square in Gniezno

5 refreshment stations along the route, including water and isotonic drink
additional: The time limit for completing the half marathon is 3 hours and 30 minutes. Timing is provided by chips attached to race bibs. The organizer provides coach transport to the start in Ostrów Lednicki. The race pack includes safety pins for attaching the bib, a medal at the finish and a recovery meal. Registration and race-pack collection take place at the sports hall of II LO in Gniezno on 19 September from 15:00 to 20:00 and on 20 September from 7:00 to 9:00. The participant limit is 2,000; minimum age is 18. Travel by coach or own transport.

The races take place on cross-country courses, giving participants the chance to compete amid beautiful autumn scenery. The event is part of the Grand Prix in cross-country running and Nordic walking, promoting physical activity and a healthy lifestyle in the local community.

Autumn scenery suited to running and Nordic walking
An event included in the Grand Prix in cross-country running and Nordic walking

The event offers a range of distances from 10 km to 100 km, following challenging mountain routes with beautiful views and natural terrain. It attracts both recreational and experienced runners, offering unique challenges and a distinctive atmosphere. The organizers ensure the event runs professionally and that participants are safe.

Picturesque views of the Beskids
Natural forest and rocky terrain
additional: Start and finish in Węgierska Górka. The routes pass through the Beskids over varied terrain. The event takes place on 2–3 October 2026. The event offers different participant categories, as well as an archive of results and event partners.

name: ING Biegnij Warszawo
description: ING Biegnij Warszawo is one of Poland’s best-known running events, bringing together thousands of participants in the heart of the capital every year. The race takes place on the first Saturday of October and features a 10-kilometre route through Warsaw’s most iconic locations. The FUNRUN format focuses on the joy of movement, without pressure or competition, and encourages participants to run, walk or jog at their own pace. Along the route, participants are supported by music zones, cheering spectators and motivating partner stations, and everyone receives a commemorative Nike Dri-FIT T-shirt and a medal at the finish.
course_highlights: A 10 km route through Warsaw’s most atmospheric and iconic locations
Music zones and cheering spectators along the entire route
A hydration station halfway through the distance and comprehensive medical support
additional: The race pack includes a Nike Dri-FIT T-shirt with a commemorative print, a race bib with a timing chip, partner gifts and a commemorative medal. Race packs can be collected at Legia Sports Bar at Legia Warsaw Stadium from 29 September to 3 October 2026; early collection is recommended. Drivers using the food and drink facilities get 2 hours of free parking. The route is certified by PZLA and is beginner-friendly. The event brings together more than 6,000 participants, and the route has been changed to the right bank of the Vistula, with strong involvement from ING employees and a charity fundraiser.

Scenic terrain of the Masovian Lowland

location: Rytro, Nowy Sącz County, Lesser Poland Voivodeship, Poland
description: The 13th Podbieg na Makowicę is a 10 km mountain race taking place on October 3, 2026, in Rytro, Małopolska. The course has a challenging profile with uphill sections, making it an excellent challenge for runners who enjoy mountain routes. The organizers encourage participants to prepare using dedicated training plans tailored to different experience levels. The event is part of the TreningBiegacza.pl running calendar, which promotes running and supports runners in their preparations.

Challenging uphill sections
Scenic views around Rytro

description: The JuraRun Running Festival is a unique sporting event held in the heart of the Kraków-Częstochowa Upland, bringing together a passion for running, competition and the satisfaction of pushing your limits. In 2026, as many as 9 different running events are planned, with distances ranging from 5 km to over 100 km, as well as Nordic Walking and a night run. The routes pass through scenic landscapes, limestone rocks, forests and Jurassic hills, offering both technical challenges and beautiful views. The festival is open to runners of all ability levels and features a varied programme of events and attractive race packages.

JuraRun ULTRA 100+ is an ultra of over 100 km with minimal asphalt, requiring technical skill and endurance

additional: Starts take place in waves; for example, the JuraRun Night 10+ night run starts at 21:00. The race package includes, among other things, timekeeping, medical support, aid stations, a medal, a post-race meal and the option to purchase personalised technical apparel. Ultra routes have mandatory equipment that is checked before the start. During the festival, there are activities, an expo and talks on running and a healthy lifestyle. 9 sporting events, options to split participation into stages, talks and meetings about running and a healthy lifestyle, online registration

name: Festiwal Biegowy Silesia Marathon 2026
description: Silesia Marathon is the largest running event in Silesia. In 2026, it will take place as a three-day running festival. Participants can choose from a range of distances, including the marathon, half marathon, ultramarathon, and 10 km and 5 km races. The finish line is at the iconic Silesian Stadium, giving the event a distinctive character. It is not only a competition, but also an unforgettable experience and a celebration of the running community.
course_highlights: Finish at the Silesian Stadium in Chorzów
A range of distances: marathon, half marathon, ultramarathon, 10K and 5K
A three-day running festival with many attractions
additional: In 2026, Silesia Marathon will take place as a three-day running festival for the first time, offering more distances and options to choose a race suited to participants’ abilities and goals. Participants receive a race pack, including a free technical T-shirt when they enter the half marathon, marathon or ultramarathon. Registration opens on 15 December 2025. The event includes various race categories, with regulations and courses available on the website. Participants can expect support and attractions throughout the event.

name: 25 Poznań Maraton
description: The 25th Maciej Frankiewicz Poznań Marathon is the jubilee 25th edition of the classic 42.195 km distance, taking place on 4 October 2026 in Poznań. For a quarter of a century, the race has brought together thousands of runners and spectators, offering a new, attractive course that starts and finishes at the Poznań International Fair grounds. The organisers provide professional medical support, timekeeping and a comprehensive race pack. It is a special sporting celebration, with enthusiastic support from Poznań’s spectators and a rich tradition.
course_highlights: A new, attractive course starting and finishing at the Poznań International Fair grounds
The classic marathon distance of 42.195 km
A jubilee 25th edition with a rich tradition and enthusiastic support from local spectators
additional: The race pack includes a race number with a chip, safety pins, sponsor materials, professional timekeeping, medical support, and refreshment stations offering isotonic drinks, water, chocolate, fruit and sugar. The organiser provides free overnight accommodation for 600 people in POSiR sports halls on 3–4 October 2026; participants must bring their own mats and sleeping bags. There are numerous car parks near the Poznań International Fair grounds, with different rates. OK Poznań programme participants receive a 25% discount, while people aged 60 and over receive a 50% discount. The official marathon T-shirt can be ordered until 1 September 2026 for PLN 70. Registration is open until 1 October 2026. Discounts are available for seniors and programme participants, along with official merchandise and sportswear. Side events include Poznań Run Expo and the Kids Marathon.

It’s a great opportunity to combine sport with the beauty of nature and active recreation.

The event supports the protection of endangered animal species living in Poland, and participants can also run virtually on a route of their choice. The main race consists of two laps of approximately 5 km each. Children’s and youth races are also held. All participants receive commemorative medals, and the top runners receive prizes from sponsors.

The race is part of initiatives promoting nature conservation and an active lifestyle.

description: The XRUN Grand Finale is a mountain trail race taking place on 4 October 2026 in Żegiestów-Zdrój, with its base at the CECHINI Spa House. Participants can choose from four distances: 40 km with 1,800 m of elevation gain, 28 km with 1,300 m of elevation gain, 18 km with 900 m of elevation gain, and shorter distances for children. The routes pass through scenic mountains, featuring technical descents and challenging climbs, making the race appealing to fans of mountain challenges. The event is a great way to round off the running season, combining intensity with the beauty of mountain nature.

additional: The race office and the start/finish for all distances are at the CECHINI Spa House. Age categories for children aged 3 to 15, with distances of 150, 300, 500, 800 and 1,000 m. The routes pass through Pusta Wielka, Jaworzynka, the PTTK mountain hut above Wierchomla and other mountain trails. Participants must be at least 16 years old; younger participants need written permission from a guardian. The event also includes KIDS family races and is the finale of a series of mountain races in Poland, bringing the season to a close at the highest sporting and community level.

name: 12. PKO Cracovia Półmaraton Królewski
description: The Cracovia Royal Half Marathon is an international half marathon held in Kraków, a city with a thousand-year history and the former seat of Polish kings. The race attracts thousands of participants from around the world, combining a passion for sport with sightseeing at historic sites. The finish inside the impressive TAURON Arena Kraków delivers unforgettable excitement and cheers from the spectators. The event is part of the Royal Running Triad and the Polish Half Marathon Crown, underscoring its prestige and standing among runners.
course_highlights: The course runs through the streets of Kraków, a city with a rich history and royal heritage
The finish is inside Poland’s largest indoor sports and entertainment venue, TAURON Arena Kraków
The race is part of the prestigious Royal Running Triad and the Polish Half Marathon Crown
additional: Race packs are collected at designated locations in accordance with the Run with Class rules. In 2026, the race is part of the Royal Running Triad, where participants can earn a special medal and trophy for completing all three races in the series. The event includes various running categories, including the half marathon and other distances, with registration available online and at the race office. The race takes place in an urban setting, with routes passing through attractive parts of Kraków.

name: Wzgórzowa Trzynastka

description: Wzgórzowa Trzynastka is a 13 km trail race held in the picturesque surroundings of Chrząszczyce. The route follows municipal roads and crosses a military training area between Chrząszczyce, Domecko, Opole-Winów and Górki. The event promotes a healthy, active lifestyle and running as a form of recreation. In addition to the individual race, it also features relay races, a uniformed services category and a family team orienteering challenge. The start and race office are in Chrząszczyce, and the participant limit is 300.

Picturesque surroundings of Chrząszczyce, Domecko, Opole-Winów and Górki

Trail race, relays, children's orienteering game, fundraising for the stadium.

name: 30 Bieg Przełajowy o Nóż Komandosa
location: Stadion miejski, Lubliniec, Silesian Voivodeship, Poland
description: The 30th Commando’s Knife Cross-Country Race is a prestigious running event held under the honorary patronage of the Bishop of the Polish Military, Dr. Wiesław Lechowicz. The race takes place at the Municipal Stadium in Lubliniec and is intended for soldiers and uniformed-service officers, who compete in full field uniform. The event aims to determine the uniformed services’ cross-country champions, promote mass-participation running, and foster integration among uniformed-service communities. The course runs along the street in front of the stadium and finishes on the stadium track. The women’s race starts at 12:00 and the men’s at 12:27.
course_highlights: Start and finish at the Municipal Stadium in Lubliniec
The course follows the street in front of the stadium and finishes on the stadium track
Runners compete in full field uniform and special tactical boots
additional: All participants compete in the OPEN category, with no age-group divisions. Full long-sleeved field uniform is required, along with special tactical boots that rise above the ankle and are in military colours. Additional civilian clothing is allowed only if its colours match the uniform. The race judge decides whether it is permitted. Participants must be active-duty or reserve soldiers or uniformed-service officers. Cross-country terrain; online registration; participant limit through 15.09.2026; entry fees from 150 zł to 200 zł; start at 12:00 at the Municipal Stadium in Lubliniec.

The races take place in the scenic surroundings of Mysłowice, creating a friendly atmosphere and a running community. The routes are marked and follow well-known trails as well as quiet, less-traveled paths, allowing both experienced ultrarunners and beginners to enjoy every kilometre. The event is also an opportunity to bring the running community together and promote the region.
